We’re looking for an accomplished programme leader to head our Coal Project Delivery team and take ownership of a £20m to £30m annual capital investment programme. You’ll lead projects that improve water quality, protect communities and create lasting environmental benefits.

You’ll combine strategic leadership with a strong record of delivery at scale. You’ll know how to set direction, build organisational confidence and bring people together around complex priorities, while maintaining a clear focus on outcomes.  You'll join an established and highly capable team, with genuine scope to shape future delivery, influence organisational priorities and leave a lasting legacy through nationally significant environmental projects.

You'll lead an established team of experienced project and programme professionals with a strong track record of delivering complex environmental projects.

We welcome applications from leaders in infrastructure, water, utilities, highways, environmental delivery, construction and other complex programme environments. Mining experience is not essential. What matters is your ability to lead people, shape strategy and deliver major programmes successfully.  Specialist knowledge of our work can be developed.

You’ll bring:

* A track record of leading complex capital programmes or portfolios at scale
* Experience building and developing high-performing delivery teams
* The credibility to influence senior stakeholders and navigate competing priorities
* Strong commercial judgement and confidence operating within governance and risk frameworks
* Experience overseeing significant budgets, delivery partners and supply chains
* The ability to turn strategic ambitions into a deliverable programme that achieves real outcomes

This opportunity will suit someone motivated by purpose, scale and influence, and by the chance to deliver work that makes a tangible difference to communities and the environment.

## About The Role

As Head of Project Delivery (Coal), you’ll have significant ownership of one of the Mining Remediation Authority’s largest capital programmes, leading an established and highly capable team of project and programme professionals.

Alongside ensuring successful delivery, you’ll help shape the programme’s future direction. You’ll strengthen relationships across the organisation, build a sustainable pipeline of future work and influence how we deliver long-term environmental and community value.

Working with senior colleagues across Operations, Technical, Engineering, Planning and Environmental teams, you’ll provide the leadership, governance and strategic oversight needed to deliver a diverse and complex portfolio safely and effectively.

In this influential role, you will:

* Set the strategic direction for the Coal Project Delivery programme
* Lead, develop and empower a team of project and programme professionals
* Take ownership of performance across a £20m to £30m annual capital programme
* Provide assurance and oversight across budgets, governance, risk and delivery
* Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, customers and delivery partners
* Strengthen the long-term programme pipeline and future delivery capability
* Champion innovation, continuous improvement and delivery excellence
* Play a key role in the leadership and future direction of the Environment Directorate

This is an opportunity to lead at scale, influence strategic decisions and shape a programme with clear national, environmental and community impact.

Senior Associate - Venture & Growth (m/f/d)

**Join the team rewriting the rules in private markets.**

Our team combines finance veterans with talent from tech, consulting, law and industries you'd never expect. Headquartered in Berlin, we operate from eight offices across Europe, the US and Asia.

If you're ready to build what's next in private markets, let's talk.

**Mission:**

Turn Moonfare's access to the world's leading venture managers into a steady, well-underwritten flow of single-company investments our clients can actually buy.

**About the role:**

A significant share of Moonfare's AuM sits in venture and growth, and the direct side of it, co-investments and secondaries in VC-backed companies, is where the business is growing fastest. Right now that dealflow arrives faster than we can review it, which puts the deployment of our proprietary funds at risk and caps how far the direct platform can scale. The scope of this role begins the moment an opportunity reaches us and ends when the deal closes, so operations sits outside it, as does the client raise itself. Your first year is weighted towards screening, pipeline and diligence, with the sourcing and business development side building from there as your market view and relationships deepen. You will work alongside senior members of the team rather than alone, and what moves forward is decided together.

**The team:**

Venture & Growth sits inside Moonfare's Investment team and runs two connected things. One is a multi-manager vehicle making primary fund investments into leading VC and growth managers across the US and Europe, where we have historically backed Founders Fund, a16z, Accel, Lightspeed, Khosla and General Catalyst. The other is the direct programme of co-investments and secondaries that those manager relationships generate, which is where this role's centre of gravity sits. You will report to the Head of VC & Direct Investing and work daily with the commercial team, who depend on you for qualified dealflow, and alongside Legal and Operations to close deals and launch the SPVs we distribute on the platform.

**You will:**

* **Own the direct deal pipeline.** Everything from the moment an opportunity reaches us through to close is yours to run, so nothing sits unscreened and no access window quietly closes while we are still deciding.
* **Screen inbound co-investments and secondaries, and bring a view to the team.** You run the first pass on what reaches us and form a position on it. What progresses is decided together with the Head of VC & Direct Investing and the wider team, so the value of your screen lies in the quality of the argument you bring to that conversation and in how sharply you separate the two or three worth our time from the rest.
* **Run diligence on direct deals.** The core of it is judgement on the business itself: how good the company is, how strong the founding team is, how large and how contested the market is, and whether the thesis survives contact with the evidence. The technical layer sits underneath, with cap table analysis, preference stacks and waterfalls, and pricing and NAV work on secondary positions, so we know exactly what we are buying and at what price. You will do this with support from senior members of the team, and contribute to primary fund diligence alongside the direct mandate.
* **Author the investment memos that go to IC.** The committee decides on what you put in front of it, so a memo with a gap in it, an inaccuracy, or a risk nobody spotted becomes a decision made on the wrong basis.
* **Build the market view, and then the market position.** Relationships with intermediaries, GPs and, over time, founders are what get us into constrained opportunities and keep us current on where secondaries are pricing. This part of the role grows as you do, and watching how competitors structure and go to market belongs to it, because that is what keeps us competitive on price.
* **Help make the process repeatable.** You will refine how we diligence direct deals and contribute to the sourcing, screening and monitoring tooling behind it, including AI-enabled approaches, so the volume we can handle is not capped by how much a person can read.
* **Turn deals into something our clients can buy.** The commercial team depends on this seat for qualified dealflow and for support packaging opportunities into investor-ready materials. Fund deployment runs at the pace this work sets.

**The next Moonfarian:**

* **Four or more years centred on venture and growth investing.** That comes along one of two paths. Either direct investment expertise, sourcing and diligencing investments in technology companies at a venture capital, growth equity or crossover fund, or an allocator seat focused on VC and growth where you have underwritten co-investments hands-on. Directly relevant adjacent backgrounds include TMT and technology investment banking, tech-focused private equity or software buyout, corporate development or corporate VC at a technology company, and consulting with a tech or commercial diligence focus. What matters most is a demonstrable track record of hands-on deal work: screening opportunities, running diligence, and taking a view through to a decision.
* **A network in venture you can already use.** This one is non-negotiable. Relationships with GPs, intermediaries such as placement agents and bankers, and other LPs and co-investors, enough to get us access to constrained opportunities, support diligence and track spin-out candidates. You do not need the network of someone twice your experience. You do need a real one, and you will build a much larger one here.
* **Investment judgement you can defend.** You form a view on a company and argue it, including the case against. You can read a business and a founding team, size a market and test a thesis against what the evidence actually supports. You are genuinely fluent in emerging technology and can develop conviction on themes and business models, with AI front of mind but not the only lens. You assess attractiveness quickly on limited or imperfect information, you are comfortable with financial modelling and market analysis, and you know your way around cap tables, preference stacks and waterfalls, secondary pricing, VC term sheets and SPV mechanics. You can hold several live opportunities at once and prioritise sharply between them.
* **An entrepreneurial instinct, which matters here as much as the investing.** This one is non-negotiable too. This is a builder's seat as much as an investor's. You want a hand in structuring, go-to-market, process design and the operational scaffolding of a business line that is still being built. Your AI fluency goes past using the tools to designing processes around them.
* **Communication that works in three different rooms, and relationships that outlast any one deal.** You can pitch and tailor to an investment committee, to a commercial team, and to clients, and prepare the reports and presentations each of them needs. Just as important is what you build over time with GPs and intermediaries, the standing that makes them think of us when something scarce comes up, because that is what turns a contact list into access. Excellent written and spoken English is essential.

**How the role is measured:**

* Deals sourced, screened, and taken through to IC.
* Timely deployment of Moonfare's proprietary funds, such as the Moonfare Technology Fund.
* Allocation secured with GPs and intermediaries, meaning access we would not otherwise have had.
* Whether IC can decide on your memos without rework, and whether risks surface in diligence rather than after close.
* Capital raised on direct deals and the performance ultimately generated. These are programme outcomes you contribute to rather than own alone, and they are read that way.

You will monitor and maintain these relationships, spending time with installers to understand how products are fitted in practice, how technical guidance is applied and where opportunities exist to improve quality, consistency, capability and customer outcomes.

You will help strengthen our understanding of adaptation compatibility and how adaptations interact with the base vehicle. Navan is looking for a **Strategy & Operations Manager** to help drive execution across Specialty Travel & Events. * Develop reporting that gives leaders and cross-functional teams a clear view of performance and progress.
* Leverage these insights to inform executive decisions.

* Strong project management skills and a track record of delivering through others without relying on formal authority.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with senior stakeholders.
* Comfort operating in a fast-changing environment with competing priorities.
* High emotional intelligence, discretion, resilience, and a collaborative working style.

# Manager, Technical Account Management

The Manager Technical Account Management is responsible for leading, developing, and supporting a high-performing team of Technical Account Managers while maintaining their own portfolio of strategic customers. Working alongside a peer TAM Manager, this role helps drive consistency, customer satisfaction, service quality, and continuous improvement across the global TAM function spanning the United Kingdom, Netherlands, Australia, and Manila.   
  
This is a player-coach role, balancing people leadership with hands-on customer engagement. The role holder directly manages a team of 5-6 TAMs while personally owning a portfolio of 10-12 customers as a Technical Account Manager.

The Manager Technical Account Management ensures TAMs are successfully executing their responsibilities, delivering measurable customer outcomes, driving customer retention, and maintaining high standards of technical and service excellence. The role also acts as a key member of the Client Services leadership team, contributing to strategy, operational improvements, resource planning, and talent development across the global TAM organisation.

## Key Responsibilities

* **Lead, coach, and develop a team of 5-6 Technical Account Managers**, ensuring high performance, engagement, and career growth.
* **Partner with the peer Manager Technical Account Management to jointly lead the global TAM function**, driving consistency across teams located in the UK, Netherlands, Australia, and Manila.
* **Maintain direct ownership of a portfolio of 10-12 customers as a Technical Account Manager**, acting as a strategic technical advisor and executive stakeholder contact.
* **Drive customer retention and satisfaction**by ensuring TAMs consistently deliver measurable customer outcomes, value realisation, and exceptional service experiences.
* **Oversee the quality and consistency of TAM deliverables**, including technical roadmaps, TAM Scores, Quarterly Business Reviews, health checks, and continuous improvement plans.
* **Act as the senior escalation point**for complex customer, service, and technical issues, ensuring timely resolution and effective stakeholder management.
* **Manage team capacity, utilisation, and resource allocation**, balancing customer demand with operational priorities and employee wellbeing.
* **Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders**, including Service Delivery Management, SOC Operations, Professional Services, Sales, and Client Services leadership teams.
* **Contribute to the strategy, development, and continuous improvement of the global TAM function**, including processes, methodologies, tooling, reporting, and best practices.
* **Support business growth and portfolio expansion**by identifying opportunities to improve customer security maturity, increase service adoption, and strengthen long-term customer partnerships.

## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

* Proven experience in **cybersecurity, managed security services, or IT services leadership**.
* Significant experience in a **customer-facing technical role** (e.g., Technical Account Manager, Security Consultant, Service Delivery Manager, Customer Success Manager, or similar).
* Demonstrated experience **leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams**.
* Preference: Experience managing **distributed or global teams** across multiple geographies and time zones.
* Ability to engage and influence **senior customer stakeholders and executives** including CISOs, Heads of Security, CIOs, and senior IT leadership.
* Strong understanding of **SOC operations, threat detection, incident response, and managed security services delivery**.
* Ability to understand and advise on **end-to-end customer environments**
* Experience with security technologies such as **SIEM, EDR** and **SOAR**
* Ability to drive **customer retention, customer satisfaction, and long-term strategic partnerships**.
* Proven experience building and governing **technical roadmaps, strategic improvement plans, and customer success initiatives**.
* Strong ability to **interpret security metrics and performance data** and translate them into clear, risk-based recommendations and executive narratives.
* Experience delivering and coaching others in the delivery of **Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs)** and executive-level presentations.
* Proven ability to balance **operational leadership, people management, and direct customer ownership**within a player-coach environment.
* Experience driving **continuous improvement initiatives**, including process optimisation, automation adoption, service maturity, and operational excellence.
* Excellent communication, coaching, mentoring, and stakeholder management skills.
* Familiarity with **service management frameworks** and operational governance practices (e.g., ITIL, KPI/SLA management, customer success methodologies).
* Relevant certifications such as **CISSP, CISM, Security+, ITIL, cloud security, or leadership qualifications** are desirable.
* Proactive, accountable, and customer-focused leader with a strong sense of ownership and a commitment to developing people and delivering exceptional customer outcomes.

* **Financial & Investment Benefits**: Enjoy peace of mind with our Pension, Life Assurance, and Share Save Scheme.

**Department**

**Projects**

* Acting as Head of Department on site, heading up the technical team to deliver projects to the highest standard, supporting your colleagues and clients as required. This will involve you spending periods of time away from home, some of which may be prolonged depending on the project requirements.

* You are expected to travel to site or other offices where applicable both in the UK and Worldwide.

Your Role & Team in a Nutshell
As a Product Engineer, you will turn new small household appliance ideas into products that are ready for launch under the Breville brand as well as other global brands in other countries. You'll lead the engineering side of new product development projects, making sure products meet expectations for performance, quality and cost. Working closely with colleagues across Programme Management, Marketing, Industrial Design, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory and Supply Chain, you'll solve technical challenges and help bring innovative products to market. You'll take ownership of your work, use the latest engineering and AI-enabled tools, and play an important role in delivering successful launches. You will be part of the R&D team of seven and work in a hybrid working model.
We will help you achieve your goals and develop by providing regular feedback and access to online training courses.
 
Your Key Responsibilities:
Develop innovative products that meet customer needs, financial goals, and industry and regulatory requirements. Translate customer insights and product use feedback into clear technical specifications.
Lead multiple new product development (NPD) projects through Newell's Stage-Gate process. Define engineering timelines, achieve key milestones, and deliver products on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards.
Create engineering product specifications and lead the development of Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA) documentation, Design Verification Plans and Reports (DVP&R), and quality specifications.
Develop test plans and work with internal and external laboratories to validate designs against requirements. Review manufacturing trial results, test data, and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) documentation, and lead design, tooling, or process improvements based on findings.
Prepare and review Engineering Change Notices (ENCs). Lead design and technical reviews, and review CAD design models and drawings with cross-functional teams.
Create basic CAD design models, using AI-assisted design tools where appropriate, to develop early prototypes and quickly evaluate new ideas.
Conduct intellectual property (IP) searches and work with legal teams on IP clearance and patent applications.
Analyse competitor products and identify opportunities for innovation, product improvement, and cost reduction.
Work closely with teams across the business to assess product safety, manufacturability, and reliability. Drive product and process improvements, from small enhancements to large-scale cost-saving initiatives.
Investigate product complaints and provide technical support to resolve issues. Apply knowledge of materials and manufacturing processes, including injection moulding, to support product design and material selection.
 
 
What You’ll Need
Minimum:
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Plastics, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Demonstrated experience in a product development, manufacturing, or engineering environment.
Practical experience with prototyping, design validation, testing, and engineering problem-solving.
Working knowledge of 3D CAD software, preferably SolidWorks or Creo, including the ability to review 3D models and 2D engineering drawings.
Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and support projects through a structured stage-gate development process.
Your advantage:
Strong understanding of, or the ability to quickly learn, manufacturing processes used in small household appliances.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to collaborate across functions and influence stakeholders.
Experience developing consumer products and bringing new products from concept through to launch.
Familiarity with electro-mechanical products and technologies.
Exposure to AI-assisted or generative design, simulation, prototyping tools, or using AI-generated code to support concept development and testing.

Newell Brands has a strong footprint in the EMEA region, with several thousand employees spread over many corporate offices and manufacturing facilities. You might recognise some of our iconic brands, like Parker, Sistema, Spontex, Crockpot, NUK, Coleman, and Yankee Candle, to name a few.

* **Establish and lead a newly created underwriting analytics team, shaping capability, standards and strategy across NFU Mutual**

  

* **Opportunity to influence enterprise-wide data and analytics decisions**

  

* **Enjoy hybrid working, spending 20% of your time from our Stratford Upon Avon offices and up to 80% home-working**

You'll strengthen underwriting decision making through robust analytics, making credible challenges, and taking clear data ownership.

  

Leading a team of up to four colleagues, including both existing specialists and new hires, you'll establish and grow a newly formed function. Working closely with stakeholders across Underwriting, Pricing, Risk, Actuarial, Customer Data Science, Enterprise Data, Technology and Architecture, you'll ensure underwriting priorities are represented across enterprise initiatives while helping shape the future direction of data and analytics across the business.

  

This role is based in our Tiddington Head Office, just outside Stratford-Upon-Avon. However, we understand how important a positive work-life balance is, so to help you give your best, we offer great facilities when you want to be in an office environment and support to work up to 80% of your hours from home.

# Associate General Counsel - AI & Product Development

* Full-time

## Job Description

We are seeking a dynamic and technically fluent attorney to join our Privacy, Product, & AI Legal team, supporting enterprise-wide, cutting-edge initiatives in AI, product development, privacy, and data governance. This is a high-impact role with cross-functional visibility, and is ideal for a lawyer passionate about emerging technologies, with a strong foundation in product regulatory compliance and commercial contracting, who is ready to grow into a strategic legal advisor. This role supports enterprise‐wide AI initiatives by assisting in the development, governance, and implementation of safe and responsible AI systems for deployment globally.

The Associate General Counsel – AI & Product Development will play a pivotal role in supporting NIQ’s business growth and innovation roadmap, while assuring adherence to global artificial intelligence and data governance laws. This role reports directly to the Chief Privacy Officer & Global General Counsel of Data Security, Product, & AI. The individual will play a key part in developing governance frameworks for AI and product creation, assisting commercial legal teams with contracts that focus on AI and data oversight, maintaining compliance with EU and new global AI regulations, and addressing risks connected to the intersections of AI, technology, cybersecurity, privacy, and data management. They will review both new and existing AI laws to actively manage legal risks, collaborating closely with partners across legal, sales, product, engineering, data science, and compliance. Legal advice will be provided on building and implementing AI systems, preparing product documentation, onboarding new clients, and ensuring all legal requirements are met for product launches and client deliverables.  They will also partner closely with commercial lawyers and sales teams to draft, review, and negotiate commercial contract provisions focused on AI, data governance, data use, product guardrails, data licensing, and privacy, ensuring protection of NIQ data assets and enablement of NIQ commercial offerings.

**Salary**: 86700 GBP to 145234 GBP gross per year. Placement within the range will depend on objective criteria including experience, skills, and internal equity considerations.We are committed to equal pay and pay transparency. Remuneration decisions are made using gender-neutral and objective criteria.​​

**Key Responsibilities:**

Product Development 

* Advise on the creation and deployment of AI and data-driven products, ensuring compliance with global laws throughout the product lifecycle

* Collaborate with Product, Technology, Engineering, and Data Science teams to integrate data governance and responsible AI frameworks into new product initiatives

* Review and interpret global AI and data regulations applicable to product features, documentation, and client deliverables, and advise on ways to balance risk and reward for NIQ

* Prepare and maintain external-facing product documentation, such as model cards and transparency notices, for regulatory compliance and client assurance. And provide legal support for onboarding new clients and launching new products
* Support legal reviews related to the development and deployment of AI products and systems, including conducting and documenting risk assessments
* Participate optimally and constructively as a member of the team and act as a strategic partner and trusted advisor on legal and non-legal issues

Commercial Contracting 

* Serve as the legal liaison for commercial, procurement, vendor management, sales, and external partners related to AI and technology initiatives

* Draft, review, and negotiate commercial contracts focused on AI, data governance, data use, product guardrails, data licensing, and privacy, ensuring protection of NIQ data assets and enablement of NIQ commercial offerings Support procurement and vendor management teams by negotiating data processing, technology, privacy, and AI contract terms with NIQ vendors, suppliers, and partners

* Translate “tech-speak” to “legal-speak” for external counter-parties, bridging the comprehension gaps between the technical functionalities of NIQ’s products and the legal terms being negotiated, for AI model and product development, deployment, commercialization (including GenAI and data-product lifecycles). Draft AI contracting guidance, playbooks, and governance materials
* Communicate with and influence business clients at all levels of the organization, including senior management and establish proactive and trustworthy relationships with clients as well as other members of the legal organization globally

Internal Compliance Requirements 

* Provide analysis and advice on compliance with emerging global AI regulations and standards. Further develop and maintain internal policies, risk assessment procedures, and training materials for AI, product development, and data governance
* Advise and oversee regulatorily defined procedures for technical teams, including best practices, employee guidance, and awareness programs. Monitor, interpret, and ensure ongoing compliance with EU and global regulations regarding AI, data privacy, data use, cybersecurity, and data governance (e.g., GDPR, EU AI Act, US state AI laws, Japan’s AI Promotion Act, South Korea’s AI Framework Act, EU’s Data Governance Act, CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA, LGPD, PIPL).
* Document and maintain records of data processing activities, risk assessments, and compliance audits to meet regulatory and client requirements.
* Conduct systematic internal audits and risk assessments to identify and mitigate AI and product legal, data, privacy, and cybersecurity risks. And various other duties as assigned to support NIQ’s AI and product roadmaps.

Qualifications: 

* Bachelor’s degree and Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree (or international equivalent) from an accredited law school. Proof of admission to the Bar (or international equivalent), and current membership in good standing of such Bar as would permit the practice of law
* 5-10 years of combined, relevant legal experience in law firms, governmental agencies, and/or in-house legal departments for data and/or technology companies  At least 5 years of experience providing product counseling, particularly in areas involving data use, automation, or machine learning in a fast-paced, global business setting
* At least 2 years of experience advising on legal issues related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, or algorithmic decision-making systems. Proven experience in and enjoyment of complex commercial contracting, redlining, and negotiation, especially in tech, AI, privacy, or cybersecurity contexts
* Exceptional communication skills and technical fluency – the ability to simplify complex technical and data-related issues for non-technical stakeholders across functions clearly and effectively
* Proven experience with AI governance, AI ethical frameworks, GenAI, data protection/ privacy laws, and cybersecurity frameworks. Knowledge of issues affecting AI/ML, Gen AI, agentic systems, including US and EU AI regulatory compliance obligations, consumer protection, algorithmic bias /discrimination, anti-trust, employment, intellectual property, data and privacy
* Proven ability to identify risks and to comfortably make smart-risk recommendations while balancing reward and business imperatives. And proven experience supporting procurement and vendor contracting processes
* Deep knowledge of global data protection, data handling, and data classification regulations such as EU AI Act, US state AI laws, GDPR, EU Data Governance Act, etc.
* Strong organizational, proactivity, creative problem-solving, and project management skills.Sound judgment evidenced through past work.
* Ability to work independently, efficiently, and collaboratively in a global team setting, under time pressures and deadlines, within a highly matrixed, complex organization. Comfortable leading calls and working groups with technical, business, and/or senior-level stakeholders
* Proven ability to lead and influence cross‐functional teams, navigate ambiguity and change, spot issues early, and collaborate effectively with a strong team‐first mindset
* Highly motivated, intellectually curious, and comfortable managing multiple priorities under tight deadlines, with strong communication skills, emotional intelligence, positive energy, and a sense of humor

Preferred Attributes

* Background in technology, computer engineering, computer science, or data science preferred

* Experience in the consumer packaged goods or data analytics industry

* Experience with patent strategy or IP licensing in AI or software/SaaS

* Prior exposure to national security law or cross-border data compliance

* AIGP and/or CIPP certification

Our mission is to accelerate how the world engineers new hardware. Nominal's
connected test and operations platform powers the world's most advanced hardware
programs and its most ambitious startups, from spacecraft, racecars, and
autonomous vehicles to next-generation defense and energy programs. Our
customers include Anduril, Shield AI, Hermeus, Albedo, Shinkei, and Pratt Miller
Motorsports, as well as U.S. Navy and U.S. Air Force programs. Now we're
expanding across the entire hardware lifecycle, building the foundation,
AI-native applications, and agents that accelerate innovators' work and change
what's possible to build.

forward-leaning AI bets. Our mission is to unlock the bottlenecks of the
hardware lifecycle with AI. Our agents reason over physical reality, from
high-rate telemetry and test campaigns to designs and simulations, where real
test results are the ground truth their work is checked against. We believe
opinionated AI, built for the real work of hardware programs, will change how
the world engineers.

customer-focused. We build with the newest AI tools every day, and because those
tools keep changing, so do we: we stay curious and keep looking for the better
way. Our team spans data science and ML, distributed systems, search, and
knowledge systems, and we obsess over how agents can be genuinely useful to the
engineers who rely on them.

agent all run on, and set technical direction for the team that builds on it.

* Design and build the agent harness: orchestration, planning, tool calling,
memory, and background agents that run long investigations on their own.
* Own the shared tool layer that our agents and external agents (via MCP) both
use, so every capability we build works everywhere.

designs, and simulations, including sensor data far too large to fit in a
context window.
* Make model choice a decision, not a dependency: routing, cost, latency, and
fallbacks across frontier models.

how the context layer grows.
* Set the architecture other engineers build on, and raise the bar through
design reviews and mentorship.

* 8+ years building production systems, including real experience shipping LLM
or agent systems to users.
* Strong distributed-systems and backend fundamentals; you've owned systems
where reliability mattered.

failure handling) and the judgment to change them when data says so.
* A track record of setting technical direction across a team and raising the
bar for the engineers around you.

day, and stay curious and open to better ways of working. The tools keep
changing, and so do we.

* You've built an agent harness or LLM platform that other engineers or
customers build on, at an AI-native company.
* You've shipped long-running, autonomous agents to production and know where

infrastructure.

Nordhealth is a remote-first company, headquartered in **Helsinki, Finland.** Our 430+ employees work either remotely or from offices/collaboration hubs. While our market presence is currently strongest in the Nordics, our customer base is rapidly growing in North America and Europe, with clients in the US, UK, Spain and many others. For more information, visit our company’s website at www.nordhealth.com

#### **About the role**

**We are here to create great healthcare products. That’s at our very core, but it’s the people who make companies great, not the other way around**. We spend more time with our co-workers than anyone else in our lives. Being part of an exceptional team is not only important for your personal mindfulness but key for your professional progression.

We’re looking for a smart, entrepreneurial and hungry salesperson early in their career to drive new business in the UK. You’ll own the full sales cycle, from first contact to closing, with real responsibility for winning new SME customers in the regions of London, South East England, South West England, East of England and Wales!   
  
Why should you join? You'd learn the whole sales process, see the direct results of your work and earn greater responsibility as you prove yourself. In addition to the positive impact you'd made, helping veterinary teams spend more time caring for animals.🚀

#### **Your key responsibilities include**

* Win new customers among independent veterinary clinics and growing clinic groups across the UK.
* Build your own pipeline through targeted prospecting, calls, emails, events and clinic visits.
* Understand each clinic’s needs, present engaging virtual demos and tailor Provet packages to the problems they need to solve.
* Lead negotiations, close deals and hit monthly sales targets.
* Record activities, next steps and accurate forecasts in our CRM.
* Coordinate with the onboarding team to give new customers a smooth start and clear expectations.
* Work with marketing and analytics to improve targeting, outreach and conversion

You might be an exceptional graduate, an SDR ready for more ownership, or in your first few years of sales or another customer-facing role. Show us evidence of ability through your work, studies, a business you’ve built or another demanding pursuit. In addition:

* Smart and curious. You learn quickly, ask good questions and explain complex ideas simply.
* Hungry to achieve. You set high standards, work hard and can show where you’ve pushed yourself to achieve something difficult.
* Entrepreneurial. You take initiative, find ways around obstacles and create opportunities without waiting to be told.
* Resilient and coachable. You handle rejection, ask for feedback and put it into practice.
* Good with people. You listen carefully, build trust and follow through on your commitments.
* Veterinary software experience is not required.
* You should be **based in London and willing to travel** to UK customers.
* You're holding a **UK driving license.**

#### **What’s in it for you?**

At Nordhealth, we do things a little bit differently. We value continuous improvement, diverse teams and autonomy which drive our collaboration. Our global healthcare domain is rapidly developing and we are seeking colleagues who enjoy working in this type of environment. 🌎  
  
In addition, we offer:

* The chance to work in a meaningful industry and in a fast-growing, global company on a path to changing digital healthcare
* Competitive compensation and benefits
* Learning and professional growth opportunities
* The tools you need, and enjoy using
* Frequent company events and talented colleagues from around the world

If you enjoy working in a fast-growing and international environment with the possibility to make an impact, this might be the perfect job for you. Apply now! We'll fill the position as soon as we find the right person.

Nscale is taking on the hyperscalers by building a vertically integrated GenAI cloud platform. ## **About the role**

The Director, Legal, Energy & Power Procurement, EMEA is Nscale's dedicated UK-based counsel for energy and power procurement across EMEA, reporting to the VP, Legal, Real Estate and Construction.

This is a hands-on execution role supporting the development and operation of Nscale's EMEA data centre campuses. You will lead the legal workstream for securing the power, generation capacity and energy services that underpin hyperscale AI infrastructure from early-stage power strategy and term sheets through negotiation, delivery and ongoing operation.

As Director, you will lead your own matters end-to-end, negotiate directly with utilities, generators, energy suppliers, developers and major equipment providers, and apply consistent commercial and legal positions across multiple jurisdictions. You will work closely with local external counsel where jurisdiction-specific advice is required.

* Lead the negotiation of power procurement, utility supply, grid connection, interconnection and network-use arrangements for Nscale data centre campuses across EMEA.
* Draft and negotiate power purchase agreements, sleeved and corporate PPAs, energy supply agreements, renewable-energy arrangements and related certificates or attribute procurement structures.
* Negotiate development, supply, installation and O&M agreements for on-site and behind-the-meter generation, energy storage, microgrids and critical power infrastructure.
* Support the delivery of grid-connection and energisation programmes, including capacity reservation, connection works, milestone, security and delay-risk arrangements.
* Advise on the legal and commercial allocation of energy and power risk, including pricing, volume commitments, curtailment, imbalance, change in law, force majeure, credit support and termination rights.
* Partner with real estate, construction, procurement, finance and operations teams to align power procurement with campus development schedules and operational requirements.
* Support site acquisition and development workstreams by assessing power availability, utility constraints and energy-related contractual risks.
* Maintain and improve Nscale's energy and power procurement templates, playbooks and contracting positions, adapting them for local law and market practice.
* Run counterparty comment rounds and drive consistent house positions across projects, while balancing speed, bankability and commercial outcomes.
* Coordinate energy-related insurance, guarantees and bonding requirements with the insurance team, and partner with Debt Capital Markets Legal on lender requirements for project-financed sites.
* Manage EMEA outside counsel, including scope, budgets and quality of advice.
* Monitor and advise on regulatory developments relevant to energy procurement, grid access, renewable-energy claims and data-centre power supply.

* 7+ years PQE legal experience in energy, power, infrastructure or major projects, gained in-house and/or at a top-tier law firm.
* Qualified solicitor or barrister in England and Wales, or another relevant EMEA jurisdiction, in good standing. England and Wales qualification is strongly preferred.
* Strong track record negotiating complex energy and power arrangements, including utility, grid connection, interconnection, energy supply, PPA, generation, equipment supply and O&M agreements.
* Experience supporting large-scale, mission-critical, industrial, infrastructure or energy-intensive projects.
* Experience working across multiple EMEA jurisdictions and managing local counsel effectively.
* Fluency in energy and infrastructure risk allocation, including pricing structures, capacity and volume commitments, delay remedies, credit support, performance guarantees, warranties, insurance, liability caps and dispute-resolution provisions.
* A confident first-chair negotiator, able to run multiple high-value contracts in parallel and drive them to signature.
* Ability to explain complex legal and commercial risk clearly to non-lawyers and senior stakeholders.
* Comfort working alongside real estate, construction, project finance, insurance, regulatory and technical counterparts.

* Prior experience at a hyperscaler, colocation provider, data centre developer, energy developer, utility, major contractor or infrastructure investor.
* Experience with corporate, sleeved or utility-scale PPAs and renewable-energy procurement.
* Experience with grid connection, transmission or distribution arrangements across EMEA.
* Experience with on-site generation, energy storage, microgrids or critical-power equipment.
* Project finance and bankability experience.
* Energy regulatory, permitting or environmental attribute experience.
* Additional European language skills.

**About the Team**

Spectrum Group is responsible for setting the long-term strategy for spectrum use in the UK, understanding demand from different stakeholders, and clearing, awarding and licensing the radio spectrum, which enables access to all types of wireless technologies: for example, TV, mobile, satellite, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and drones.

Radio spectrum is a vital resource used by almost everyone - consumers as well as businesses and it touches our lives every day. The spectrum connects our mobiles, wireless headphones, tablets and computers.  It enables our key fobs to unlock our cars, satellites to measure the climate and meteorologists to forecast the weather. It also ensures that concerts and productions are seen and heard.  TV and radio broadcasting would not exist without it.  Without access to vital spectrum, police, fire, ambulance, the coastguard, and air traffic control would not be able to communicate.

The Space Spectrum Authorisation and Policy team consist of around 30 colleagues –comprising a mix of policy, regulatory and licensing roles. We help to create and update the authorisations that enable access to spectrum for innovative services in the UK, including in the satellite, drones and maritime sector.

  

**Purpose of the Role**

The successful candidate can expect to undertake a range of activities to support innovative access to spectrum, with a particular focus on the space and satellite sector where new services and technologies are emerging at a rapid pace.

This role will:

* Provide policy and delivery leadership on new requests for spectrum access for innovative satellite/space services. You will lead a range of specialist colleagues to assess new requests, identify how new services can be enabled and issue appropriate authorisations, including policy consultations in some cases;
* Coordinate Spectrum Group’s engagement with space stakeholders, including leading engagement on new requests.

You will be organised and effectively lead groups of colleagues to deliver to timelines, using attention to detail and clear stakeholder engagement to identify and resolve issues.  You will work closely with a range of colleagues including economists, lawyers and engineers to assess requests and ensure applicants have met requirements where relevant. You will drive the development and drafting of internal decision notes, and external consultations and decisions in some cases. You will be expected to work independently and within a team, reporting to a Principal Policy Advisor.

There will be opportunities to work with different sectors and stakeholders, and represent Ofcom’s position to them, with an emphasis on proactive external engagement to gather new market insights to inform our policy approaches.

  

**Your key responsibilities**

Tasks will be varied and would suit an individual that takes an active approach to planning and developing projects and excels in bringing a range of individuals together to deliver as a team.  This role will also suit an individual who is comfortable engaging with detailed (often technical) issues that impact on policy solutions and communicating effectively both verbally and in writing with senior internal and external stakeholders.

  

Effective collaboration with other parts of Ofcom is critical to the role, particularly with economists, lawyers and technical specialists.

**Key aspects of the role are:**

* Lead and project manage end to end licensing processes for innovative new technologies with a high degree of autonomy, working with technical colleagues, economists and lawyers to interrogate applications, identify potential policy problems and solutions to grant authorisations in a timely way.
* Where relevant, develop and draft policy consultations and decisions, considering responses in determining whether Ofcom should grant a licence.
* Stakeholder engagement - collaborate with colleagues in other parts of Ofcom (including policy, authorisation, international) to understand stakeholder’s needs, coordinate engagement and identify where we need to be consistent with our approach and communications. As part of this you would help to manage Spectrum Group’s  overall relationships with key space stakeholders, leading engagement on our licensing processes and helping to share trends and information across the wider policy and operational functions.
* Consider how policy and procedures might be improved to simplify the application process for both applicants and Ofcom.

  

**The skills, knowledge and experience you will need for success**

  

* **Empowering Development:** Leads, mentors, and motivates colleagues while ensuring accountability and embedding best practice in line with organisational policies.
* **Owning Accountabilities:** delivery-focused with ability to set up and manage projects, prioritise your own and other’s resources and produce high-level deliverables on time to meet tight deadlines.
* **Harmonising Work:** an ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines and with a range of experts, understanding and balancing different skills to build a common goal and deliver joined up, robust policy solutions.
* **Articulating Ideas:** first-rate communications skills, in particular the ability to explain complex issues clearly both in writing and orally, adapting content to suit a variety of audiences.
* Experience in project management or policy development working in government, regulation or a relevant sector.

  

**Desirable Skills, Knowledge and experience**

* An understanding of spectrum management principles or a broader understanding of wireless communications is helpful but can be developed over time in the role.

**Inclusive hiring at Ofcom**

  

At Ofcom, our mission is clear: to make communications work for everyone. To achieve that, our people must reflect the diversity of the UK, in background, identity and experience. 

  

We believe innovation thrives when difference is valued and everyone feels empowered to contribute their ideas and perspectives. **ABOUT OLIPOP**

At OLIPOP, we’re on a mission to positively impact consumer health at scale. And we’re doing it through something simple: soda. But not just any soda, a new kind of soda: one that’s delicious, refreshing, and actually good for you.

This mission is deeply personal for our CEO, Co-Founder, and Formulator, Ben Goodwin. Like many of us, Ben grew up consuming the Standard American Diet: lots of soda and processed foods that prioritized convenience over nutrition. But at 14, he took his health into his own hands. After making significant changes to his nutrition and exercise, he lost 50 pounds and saw a transformation in his energy, mood, and emotional clarity.

Those changes sparked a deep curiosity about the connection between nutrition and health. Ben became a relentless student of the gut microbiome and the ways it supports overall wellness. The more he discovered, the more passionate he became about finding credible, science-backed ways to make consumer health accessible to everyone.

The mission was clear. The vehicle? Less so. After exploring the possibilities, Ben landed on an unexpected yet familiar choice: soda. It was something he loved as a kid, and he knew millions shared that same nostalgia. But this wouldn’t be just any soda. With most Americans falling short on daily fiber, Ben set out to create a version with more fiber and less sugar, one that was perfectly balanced. The result? A deliciously refreshing soda with 6 to 9 grams of fiber and 2 to 5 grams of sugar, delivering science-backed benefits without sacrificing the classic taste people crave.

In 2018, the first OLIPOP cans hit the shelves, bringing Ben’s vision to life with a functional soda that anyone could enjoy. And by reimagining soda, we’re also reshaping culture. That means creating products that support health for all and building a business grounded in humanistic values: empathy, integrity, and a belief in better for everyone. From the ingredients we source to the culture we foster, we’re committed to proving that business (and beverage!) can be a force for good, and that soda has the power to bring people together.

So join us, and let’s write a new American soda story together. One we can all feel good about. One OLIPOP at a time.

**THE ROLE**

OLIPOP is hiring a CX Operations Analyst to serve as the operational backbone of our Omnichannel Customer Experience organization. This is an individual contributor position built for someone who can take ownership of the systems, tooling, and cross-functional relationships that enable the broader CX team to perform at its best. 

The ideal candidate will balance meaningful project work, including AI-enabled customer service tooling and subscription experience enhancements, with the operational discipline required to keep DTC & B2B order management, fulfillment, technical tools, and fraud prevention running smoothly day to day. Success in this role requires comfort contributing to vendor strategy discussions, executing detailed system configuration work, and building reporting to help make informed decisions across the CX org. 

**RESPONSIBILITIES** 

**CX Program Management** 

Manage cross-functional CX initiatives from planning through execution, including:  

* efforts tied to new product launches and new market expansion

* Own documentation, deliverables, and stakeholder alignment across each initiative working with partners internally and externally

**Systems and Tooling Ownership** 

Own the configuration, maintenance, and continued evolution of our backend CX tools, including: 

* Rule sets, routing rules, and workflow updates as business needs evolve

* New tooling set up and maintenance

Technology includes but is not limited to Gorgias, Digital Genius, Guru, Shopify, NetSuite, Stay.ai, Rediem, Redo/Malomo, and Klaviyo. 

**Logistics and Order Operations** 

* Serve as the primary point of contact for our third-party logistics partner on B2B and DTC order management and fulfillment strategy within our ERP system

* Own the relationship with our 3PL, Amazon partner, retail.com partners, internal Supply Chain team, and others, end to end

* Partner with CX Manager and third party software provider to enhance

**Customer Journey and Subscription Experience**

**AI Enablement and Automation** 

* Lead the development and ongoing refinement of AI-powered tools for the CX organization.

* Report on tool performance and business impact, identify new automation opportunities, and serve as the primary strategic partner to our third-party AI vendor (Digital Genius), in partnership with our CX Associate

**Voice of Customer (VoC) Reporting**

* Synthesize recurring themes and customer feedback into clear, actionable insights for cross-functional partners using helpdesk (Gorgias) and review platform (Bazaar Voice) insight

* Work closely with CX Manager on ticket tagging/tracking strategy and reporting optimization

**REQUIREMENTS**

* Hands-on experience with a helpdesk platform (Gorgias experience strongly preferred), an ERP system (Netsuite), an ecommerce platform (Shopify) and 3PL relationship management
* Required: hands-on experience building, implementing, or managing conversational customer service automation tools  and workflows (e.g., ticket automation, workflow rules, or AI-assisted tooling), beyond simply operating existing solutions
* Proven experience leading or supporting cross-functional projects with competing deadlines and multiple stakeholders
* Working knowledge of ecommerce fraud and chargeback processes, or the demonstrated ability to build this expertise quickly
* Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to represent CX policy and process clearly to both internal and external audiences
* Demonstrated ability to move fluidly between high-level strategy and hands-on execution

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Familiarity with ecommerce platforms (Shopify), ERP Systems (NetSuite), and their unique support considerations

* Experience working with conversational AI tools

Sr. Manager, CX & Loyalty Marketing

We may be fully remote, but we’re anything but disconnected. OLIPOP has grown from a few passionate people around a table to a nationwide team, and we’ve done it without losing our collaborative spirit or sense of purpose.

Connection here is intentional. From cross-functional projects and IRL offsites to thoughtful Slack threads and spontaneous gifs, we make the effort to stay close, even across time zones. ### Senior Software Engineer

Product Delivery - London, Greater London (Remote)

---

About OneView Commerce

Retailers with thousands of shops have had two options, and neither is good. Web-native platforms move fast but were never built for a shop floor. Legacy store systems were built for the shop floor but take a year to change anything. OneView Commerce is the third option: a headless commerce platform for physical retail that lets the world's largest retailers innovate just as quickly as the smaller ones. We ship store experiences that deploy fast out of the box, and we give retailers the freedom to build their own on top of a headless transaction engine engineered for the physical store rather than the browser.

Our customers are global retailers who build on OneView because it lets them keep moving: new journeys, new channels, and new store formats ship continuously rather than waiting on the next multi-year programme.

Founded in 2010 to close the gap between fast-moving e-commerce and slow-moving in-store systems, OneView's founding principle is a single view of customers, orders, and inventory throughout the shopping journey. That remains our mission as we enable retailers to deliver exceptional store experiences that build loyalty.

We are a remote-first team with Viewers working across the globe, and we operate as a trusted provider of digital commerce systems for leading retailers.

Position Summary

OneView is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to take on the harder half of what a delivery team builds. The platform serves over a hundred thousand users across global retail estates, on terminals that have to keep taking payments when the connection drops and reconcile perfectly when it comes back. That is where the difficulty lives, and it is the work this role gets. Reporting to the VP of Engineering and working in a Scrum team alongside a Lead Software Engineer, you will design and build complex features and integrations end to end, from very little direction.

Senior here means three things concretely. You take the problem nobody has scoped yet and come back with something defensible. You lead reviews of other people's work and leave the code better than the review found it. And you contribute to what the team chooses: the methods, the libraries, the tooling, argued on evidence rather than preference.

You will mentor a Software Engineer, usually one at a time, and the measure is whether they got better rather than whether their tickets got closed. This is the rung below Lead Software Engineer and a deliberate step towards it, so the parts of that job you want more of are available to you.

The Lead Software Engineer owns the team's standard, its improvement agenda, and its technical direction, and you are the person they will lean on most to shape all three. Bring them the problems worth solving, argue for what should change, and take the work on. The more of it you can carry, the more of it becomes yours. We use AI throughout our day-to-day work and expect you to find uses for it we have not thought of. We also expect you to be able to do this job well if it were switched off tomorrow, because the creativity, judgement, and relationships that make the work good are yours rather than the tool's.

Responsibilities

* Design and build complex features and integration services end to end, from little direction, for a platform running continuously across thousands of shops in multiple countries.
* Take the hardest item on the team's backlog and be trusted with it.
* Own the technical design for significant pieces of work. Write it down, take it to the team and the Lead Software Engineer, and change it on the strength of the argument rather than defending it. Design in performance, security, and resilience rather than retrofitting them.
* Lead reviews of colleagues' work, and make review the place code gets better.
* Contribute to the team's choices about methods, libraries, and tooling, argue for them on evidence, and bring the Lead Software Engineer the problems worth solving.
* Work with the Product Owner to shape what gets built: challenge scope that is not worth its cost, surface the technical constraint before it becomes a surprise, and offer the cheaper option when there is one.
* Write the tests that prove your work now and catch the regression later.
* Run the technical investigations nobody else has time for: evaluate the options, prototype where that is what settles it, and come back with a recommendation the team can act on.
* Break a large piece of work into something the team can deliver incrementally, so that value reaches shops in weeks rather than at the end of a quarter.
* Estimate and sequence work honestly, and raise risk to a sprint commitment while there is still time to act on it.
* Own your work in production: instrument it, watch it, and fix it when it misbehaves. At this scale a defect that occurs one time in ten thousand happens somewhere every day.
* Mentor a Software Engineer, and make them better rather than doing their work for them.
* Take part in incident response, on-call, and post-incident review for the systems your team owns, where the clock is measured against shops that cannot serve customers.
* Document what you build well enough that somebody else can change it safely.

Required skills & experience

* 5+ years building production software, with a track record of delivering complex work independently.
* Strong in a modern typed language such as TypeScript, Go, Java, Kotlin, Python, or C#.
* Depth on either the client side, in a component framework such as React, Angular, or Vue, or on the service side.
* Builds and consumes REST and event-driven interfaces, and knows when each is the right choice.
* Public cloud experience with AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, including managed and serverless compute patterns.
* Data modelling across relational and document stores, and can explain why a query is slow.
* Test-first practice. Writes tests as part of finishing work rather than as a later phase.
* Ships through the team's CI/CD pipeline rather than around it, and can read a failing build.
* Debugs a production problem from logs, traces, and metrics rather than by guessing.
* Reviews code well. Raises the standard without becoming the reason the team is waiting.
* Works from little direction. Takes an ambiguous requirement, asks the questions that resolve it, and produces something defensible.
* Has mentored at least one engineer, and can say what changed for them.
* AI-assisted development as normal practice, and can explain every line of generated code they ship.

Preferred skills & experience

* Experience in retail technology, or another domain where software runs in physical locations under real-world constraints.
* Experience of offline or intermittently connected clients, where the transaction still has to be correct once the connection returns.
* Has owned a service or component in production over a sustained period, through its problems as well as its build.
* Performance profiling and optimisation on a live system, and can describe what they found and what they changed.
* Infrastructure as code and pipeline work, with tools such as Terraform, Pulumi, or CloudFormation.
* Mobile or cross-platform client development.
* Has influenced a technical decision beyond their own work, and can say how they made the case.
* Has built agentic or AI-assisted development workflows, and can describe what they changed about how a team works.

Why OneView Commerce

Alongside the global retailers we already serve, we have just been selected by one of the largest store networks in the world to replace their legacy store system, and are actively pursuing more of the retailers who have decided that decades of accumulated inertia is a problem worth solving properly. The person in this role will be on that work from the start.

Work of that size only moves quickly in a company built for it. Ours is. Our teams operate with real independence and the authority to set their own direction. Nobody here waits to be told what the priority is, and nobody needs a committee's permission to fix something that is plainly broken. We are always looking to change, to evolve, and to accelerate, and we do not merely encourage our people to identify what should be done differently; we expect it of them. When they do, they have the support of their team and of leadership to make the change stick.

If you have spent time in a larger organisation where you could see improvement opportunities clearly and never got the room to implement them, that is the frustration we are built to remove. We are looking for people who find that prospect exciting. If you would rather be handed a roadmap than build one, this will not be the right fit.

We're building a team that does great work and enjoys doing it, and it shows: OneView has been named one of Built In's Best Places to Work for three years in a row. Our leadership team brings decades of experience across software development, delivery, sales, and marketing, so  the independence comes with people who know the terrain and will back your judgement.

Join us as we work with global retail leaders to innovate everything.

The successful candidate will be covered two primary areas: the security of AI (protecting the organisation's own AI systems and use of AI) and AI for security (using AI to strengthen protection, detection and response). This role will sit within Cyber Security and Compliance.

**Technical ownership of AI security tool selection and deployment**

Define requirements, run structured evaluations and proofs of concept, and judge vendor claims on evidence rather than marketing.

That means measuring detection efficacy, false positive rates, latency and operational overhead. The tool categories to cover include AI security posture management, LLM guardrails and firewalls, model and supply-chain scanning, GenAI data loss prevention, and AI-enabled SOC tooling.

**Understanding the AI threat landscape**

They need a working knowledge of AI-specific attack techniques and should be fluent in the reference frameworks, mainly the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and MITRE ATLAS. Key threats include:

* Direct and indirect prompt injection
* Data and model poisoning
* Sensitive data leakage through prompts and outputs
* Model theft and extraction
* Malicious model files in the supply chain
* The growing set of risks from agentic AI, such as excessive permissions and tool misuse

They also need to understand how attackers use AI against the organisation (more convincing phishing, deepfake-enabled fraud, faster reconnaissance and exploit development) and how that changes your threat model. Shadow AI, meaning unsanctioned use of AI tools by staff, is a practical, near-term issue they should be able to discover and manage.

**Demonstrating AI in protection, detection and response**

This is where the role earns its keep with stakeholders. In protection, that might mean AI-assisted vulnerability prioritisation, secure code review, or posture analysis. In detection, it covers behavioural anomaly detection, alert triage and enrichment, and LLM-assisted threat hunting. In response, it includes AI copilots for investigation and incident summarisation, automated playbooks, and agentic response actions.

A good candidate will be clear-eyed about limits: where human-in-the-loop controls are needed, how to validate AI outputs, and how to avoid automating mistakes at speed. The ability to build or run demonstrators that show value concretely is a strong differentiator.

**Assurance and testing**

The role should include adversarial testing and red teaming of the organisation's AI systems, whether done directly or by scoping and overseeing third parties. * The UK government's AI Cyber Security Code of Practice
* NIST AI RMF
* ISO/IEC 42001

As Preply continues to scale, Engineering remains at the core of our product, growth, and future. We're expanding technical hiring across complex domains and global tech hubs - and we're looking for a Talent Acquisition Manager - Tech to help us build a hiring engine that can match that ambition.

This is a hands-on management role. You'll directly manage a team of TA Partners with full reporting lines, while also personally owning complex engineering searches. * Strong in-house recruiting experience. You've partnered closely with Engineering Directors, VPs, CTOs, or similarly senior technical stakeholders and earned their trust.
* Experience turning workforce plans into hiring strategies. You take business priorities and headcount plans and translate them into clear, sequenced, actionable hiring plans with strong process and execution discipline: operating rhythms, weekly tracking, early risk flags, multiple tracks moving in parallel.
* A track record of improving hiring systems at scale. You've raised pipeline quality, pass-through rates, sourcing performance, or hiring predictability across teams or locations, including through AI and technology.
* Experience leading calibration and quality across a large interviewer group. You've defined hiring bars and helped hiring teams make better, more consistent decisions.
* Proven people management experience in a high-growth, fast scaling environment. A strong manager who stays close to the craft. You take pride in excellent recruiting work and want to remain hands-on.
* Strong influence and communication skills. You create clarity, challenge thoughtfully, and build trust with senior stakeholders and peers.

* Fluency in English and readiness to work from Barcelona, London, or Kyiv.

*We are looking for a **Senior Data Scientist** to join our Data & Analytics team, working between home and our London office in Angel, Islington.*

**The Role**

**Data Science at PureGym influences some of the biggest decisions we make, from where we open our next gyms and how we price, to how we keep millions of members coming back.**

Our models shape real decisions across retention, pricing, customer lifetime value and estate growth, with the impact showing up in the numbers our business runs on.

We're a small, experienced team that's great at turning good ideas into working solutions quickly. You'll join people who care about doing Data Science well, and you'll see your work **used to make real commercial decisions throughout the business, not just admired in a notebook.**

As our **Senior Data Scientist**, you'll take the technical lead on the modelling behind PureGym's spatial analytics capability.

You'll help us answer some of our most commercially important questions: **where should we grow, how do our gyms fit within their local communities, and what drives the performance of different locations?**

This is a role with significant ownership. You'll take spatial and location models from prototype through to trusted, production-ready assets, ensuring they're rigorous, explainable and capable of supporting confident investment and commercial decisions.

**What you'll be doing**

* **Own the spatial and location models** that power our analytics tools, taking them from prototype through to maintained, well-documented production assets.
* Build and evolve **catchment, location and demand models** that help us understand our markets, communities and opportunities for growth.
* Partner closely with **Property and Finance**, translating commercial questions into analytical problems and ensuring our models deliver meaningful business value.
* Rigorously validate models through out-of-time testing, leakage checks, sensitivity analysis and clear measures of uncertainty, ensuring every input genuinely reflects the information available at the point a decision is made.
* Develop approaches for locations with limited historical data, using your technical judgement to determine when there is enough evidence to trust a result.
* Work with Engineering and Data colleagues to turn model outputs into **reusable, scalable data assets rather than one-off analysis or tables**.
* Partner with MLOps colleagues to deploy, monitor and retrain models, with clear ownership, versioning in MLflow and documented handover points.
* Turn complex model outputs into **clear, commercially relevant recommendations for senior stakeholders**, including being transparent about uncertainty and where a model should, and should not, be used.
* Evaluate external and third-party models with technical rigour, challenging assumptions and helping set the standard for how we assess them.
* Contribute to shared development standards and peer review, sharing knowledge so that our capability can scale and no critical model is dependent on one person.
* **Help shape the future of spatial analytics at PureGym**, identifying opportunities to improve our methods, tools and the commercial impact of our models.

**The Person**

You're an experienced Data Scientist with strong geospatial expertise who enjoys using complex data to solve **real-world commercial problems where the answer isn't always obvious**.

You're curious enough to question the data and rigorous enough to challenge an impressive-looking result when the evidence doesn't support it. You're also pragmatic: you understand that the best model isn't necessarily the most sophisticated one, but the one that's robust, explainable and genuinely helps people make a better decision.
