## 🔥Why This Role Is SO Important:

We’re looking for a Technical Solution Consultant to own the technical scoping of integrations and custom development for new and expanding customers.

You’ll make sure what we sell is clearly defined, deliverable and ready to hand over to Product and Engineering for build. You’ll translate complex technical discovery into requirements, assumptions, exclusions, acceptance criteria, responsibilities and statements of work that everyone can understand and act on.

This role is deliberately focused on pre-sales consulting, technical scoping and scope accountability. **You will not build, engineer, configure or technically test integrations or custom development.** Build and technical testing sit with Product and Engineering, while delivery sits with Implementation.

Your job is to make sure those teams receive a complete, accurate and decision-ready scope, and to remain the technical point of accountability for that scope throughout the project.

## Key Duties & Responsibilities

Let’s be clear from the start: this isn’t a role where you simply document customer requirements or pass questions between teams. You’ll challenge unclear requirements, identify delivery risk early, define what has and hasn’t been agreed and make sure technical commitments are realistic before a customer signs.

### Pre-Sales Integration Consulting and SOW Development

Leading Technical Discovery: Running discovery with prospects across HRIS, payroll, leave, time and attendance, EPOS, LMS, BI, middleware, identity and other third-party systems.

Mapping the Technical Landscape: Understanding systems of record, data flows, interfaces, dependencies, operational constraints and the customer’s wider technology environment.

Assessing Feasibility: Determining which requirements are standard, configurable, bespoke, out of scope or dependent on Product and Engineering delivery.

Defining Requirements: Creating integration and custom development requirements, field mappings, transformation rules, validation logic and exception-handling expectations to the level Engineering needs to estimate and build.

Clarifying Responsibilities: Defining customer responsibilities, vendor responsibilities, assumptions, exclusions, prerequisites and technical constraints.

Estimating Delivery: Providing directional or committed estimates, clearly stating the assumptions and confidence level behind each and validating them with Product and Engineering where required.

Supporting Commercial Scoping: Providing technical input for proposals, solution designs, commercial line items and statements of work.

Defining Acceptance: Establishing acceptance criteria, test responsibilities, delivery dependencies and cutover assumptions before contract signature.

Resolving Open Questions: Identifying unresolved technical questions and ensuring they are resolved, explicitly caveated or excluded from scope before signature.

### Handover to Product, Engineering and Implementation

Creating Handover Packs: Producing structured technical handover packs covering agreed scope, specifications, mappings, interface inventory, assumptions, exclusions, acceptance criteria, dependencies, risks and open questions.

Running Handover Sessions: Bringing Product, Engineering and Implementation together so delivery teams understand what was agreed and why.

Structuring Demand: Consolidating upcoming integration and custom development demand from Sales into clear Product and Engineering intake packages, including customer context, contractual status, reuse potential, requirements, dependencies, risks, estimated effort, urgency and the decision required.

Separating Customer Need From Product Capability: Distinguishing customer-specific requirements from reusable product capability.

Escalating Decisions: Taking Product and Engineering decisions forward with a clear recommendation and supporting evidence, then communicating agreed decisions back to Sales, Solution Consulting, Implementation and customers.

### Technical Representative for Agreed Scope

Owning Technical Accountability: Acting as the technical point of contact for the agreed scope throughout implementation.

Answering Scope Questions: Helping Implementation, Product, Engineering, customers and suppliers understand the requirements, intent and boundaries of what was agreed.

Assessing Scope Misses: Reviewing potential scope misses against the statement of work and handover pack and determining whether an issue is a scoping gap, change request, defect or out of scope.

Leading Rectification: Where a scope miss needs to be rectified, defining revised requirements, estimating the impact and taking the change through the appropriate route.

Representing Rotageek: Setting realistic expectations with customers and suppliers about what will change, when it will change and any associated cost.

Maintaining Change Control: Keeping a decision log and change record for the scope you own.

### Test Scripts, Bugs and Change Documentation

Creating Test Scripts: Working with Implementation and the customer to create test scripts and scenarios that validate delivered integrations or custom development against the agreed scope and acceptance criteria.

Covering Real-World Scenarios: Ensuring scripts consider happy paths, negative cases, duplicates, overlapping transactions, invalid data, retries, partial data and timing scenarios relevant to the scope.

Defining Test Ownership: Helping establish test data requirements and sign-off responsibilities with Implementation and the customer.

Documenting Defects: Reviewing test outcomes for items within your scope and documenting bugs and required changes clearly for Engineering, including expected behaviour, actual behaviour, evidence and reference to the agreed requirement.

Routing Issues Correctly: Distinguishing configuration, data-quality, integration, product and third-party issues so that each is routed to the right owner.

Supporting Ongoing Service: Contributing known issues and scope-related notes to the handover into Support and Customer Success.

### Customer and Supplier Engagement

Running Workshops: Facilitating technical discovery workshops, design reviews and scope-clarification sessions with prospects, customers and third-party suppliers.

Building Relationships: Working effectively with customer IT teams, payroll leads, HR teams, operations stakeholders and external system providers.

Setting Expectations: Explaining scope, dependencies, technical constraints and what will and will not be delivered.

Challenging Constructively: Questioning unclear or unrealistic requirements before they become commitments.

### Efficiency, Automation and Continuous Improvement

Creating Reusable Assets: Building and maintaining integration catalogues, partner playbooks, requirements templates, mapping packs, test script templates, SOW schedules and handover pack templates.

Using AI Responsibly: Applying AI and automation tools to improve requirements analysis, mapping, estimation, test script design and documentation.

Capturing Evidence: Recording recurring integration requirements, partner constraints and scope misses as structured evidence for Product and Engineering planning.

Improving the Process: Feeding lessons from scope misses back into templates and processes so future statements of work are more accurate.

Measuring Quality: Contributing to metrics focused on scope accuracy, rework, change requests and avoidable escalations.

## What Success Looks Like in Your First Six Months

✅ Integration and custom development feasibility, assumptions, dependencies, exclusions and responsibilities are understood before a customer signs.

📝 Statements of work contain clear technical scope, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, prerequisites and delivery assumptions.

🤝 Product, Engineering and Implementation inherit complete handover packs and can start build and delivery without reconstructing requirements.

📦 Product and Engineering receive consolidated, decision-ready demand rather than fragmented customer requests.

🔎 Scope misses are rare and, when they occur, are assessed, rectified and fed back into scoping practice quickly.

* Independent Sponsors (“IS”) are experienced dealmakers who identify, structure and lead buyouts and growth acquisitions without a committed fund behind them, raising equity deal by deal from co-investment partners as each transaction requires. Sponsors typically secure exclusivity first and syndicate equity to close, so judging equity certainty and the sponsor's ability to deliver it is central to the underwrite.
* As Senior Director, you will be a senior originator and a recognised part of ThinCats' face to market in the independent sponsor community, driving the identification, structuring and execution of IS transactions, and leading deal teams including more junior colleagues.
* You will own the client and sponsor relationship on your transactions, working within the appetite, pricing framework and standards set by the Head of Independent Sponsors, and contributing to the team's origination, profitability and return on equity targets.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Originate With Authority**

* Maintain an active network of senior level relationships with independent sponsors, their co-investment partners, intermediaries and advisers active in the UK lower mid-market.
* Act as a key “go-to” point of contact for inbound enquiries and be recognised as part of ThinCats' face to market in the independent sponsor community, generating new opportunities through targeted outbound activity.
* Qualify opportunities against IS criteria and the team's risk appetite, focusing on majority or control positions, or significant minority stakes with clearly controlling governance rights, and recognising when a transaction is better served elsewhere in the Group.

**Structure and Deliver**

* Structure, negotiate and execute the larger and more complex IS debt facilities, underwriting the target business, the sponsor's track record and their ability to deliver equity certainty to completion.
* Analyse target businesses and financial models in detail to build a thorough view of risk, and structure facilities that meet the sponsor's needs while protecting the Bank appropriately.
* Write or supervise high quality sighting and credit papers, ensuring all material risks are identified, minimised and mitigated, and presented with a clear recommendation.
* Lead the client and sponsor relationship through diligence, credit approval and legal completion, working with the Transaction Management team who drive execution, and keeping the deal moving through clear direction and fast decisions.

**Lead and Develop**

* Lead deal teams, including more junior colleagues, on your own transactions and in support of colleagues' deals more broadly.
* Maintain senior level relationships with Portfolio, Risk, Operations, Credit and Finance relevant to any given transaction.
* Serve as a role model within the team, supporting the development of less experienced team members.

**Act With Judgement on Risk, Governance and Conduct**

* Report all issues of regulatory concern to the Operations Director / Bank Legal & Compliance Director promptly and effectively.
* Maintain strong governance and conduct discipline throughout: clear rationale, strong documentation, no surprises.

## The Person

**Skills & Experience**

* Exceptional analytical skills, with the ability to manage complex issues; strong grounding in financial models and financial statements.
* In-depth knowledge of leveraged and acquisition finance structures, including negotiation of legal documentation.
* Judgement on equity certainty and syndication risk in deal-by-deal funded transactions.
* Strong track record of commercial acumen, strategic thinking, executive level reporting and effective business planning.
* Thorough comprehension of credit risk management, credit administration, loan production and servicing.

**Education/Professional Qualifications**

Shawbrook is committed to providing opportunities to all candidates, and understand that not all candidates may possess a qualification or education aligned to the role. We will assess each candidate on their individual experience and skills, and not solely on level of education.

**Key attributes**

## Role Overview

  

We are looking for an **experienced IT Project Manager to lead the end-to-end ISIT project coordination** for the start-up and roll-out of a new sauce and liquid production facility in the UK.

  

The role will be responsible for ensuring that all required IT and IS components are effectively coordinated, delivered, tested, secured and ready before factory go-live. This includes close coordination with the ERP workstream, as well as responsibility for business applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, shopfloor connectivity, manufacturing IT, testing, training, cutover and hypercare.

The IT Project Manager will act as the key coordination point between local site leadership, Group ISIT, the ERP Lead and ERP programme teams, infrastructure and operations teams, cybersecurity, application owners, engineering teams, external partners, and machine and equipment suppliers.

  

During the project, the position will be structured as follows:

* **80% of the role will be dedicated to the UK factory project**, leading the overall ISIT project coordination.
* **20% of the role will remain dedicated to IT Applications project management activities for UK**, working closely with the IS PMO Manager and the wider IT Applications team.

Following completion of the UK factory project, including the relevant go-live and hypercare activities, the position will transition to a **100% IT Applications Project Manager role for UK**, fully integrated into the Application's team.

  

## Role Purpose

The UK IT Project Manager will ensure the effective coordination and delivery of the overall ISIT scope required for the successful start-up of the new facility.

The role will coordinate dependencies between the different ISIT workstreams and ensure alignment between the factory project, local business teams and Group ISIT.

For the ERP workstream, the IT Project Manager will work closely with the designated ERP Lead and programme teams to ensure that ERP-related milestones, dependencies and deliverables are properly integrated into the overall factory project plan.

  

## Key Responsibilities

  

### UK Factory Project, 80%

* Lead the overall ISIT project plan, including scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, budget requirements and resource needs.
* Translate business and factory requirements into clear ISIT deliverables and ensure alignment across operations, supply chain, finance, quality, engineering, HR, legal and other relevant workstreams.
* Work closely with the designated ERP Lead and ERP programme teams to integrate ERP milestones, dependencies, testing, training, cutover and hypercare activities into the overall factory project plan.

* Identify and coordinate all business applications required outside the ERP environment, including ownership, configuration, licensing, interfaces, access rights, training and support models.
* Define and coordinate IT infrastructure requirements for the site, including network, Wi-Fi, cabling, firewalls, connectivity, PCs, printers, scanners, handheld devices, shopfloor terminals, label printers and other operational equipment.
* Coordinate manufacturing IT requirements related to production lines, machine connectivity, SCADA and OT environments, PLCs, production data capture, traceability, weighing, labelling, scanning and line-side terminals.

* Provide clear and regular reporting to project sponsors and key stakeholders.

**Local Investment Forum Member – Western Isles**

A Local Investment Forum is being recruited to make decisions on applications to SSEN Transmission’s local community funds in the Western Isles.  Your initial focus will be the Lewis Hub Local Fund, which will launch in late 2026 following extensive community engagement.  This fund will invest £1,060,000 over five years into local communities, with the forum also responsible for future SSEN Transmission funds in the Western Isles.  Anyone in the Western Isles can apply. As much of the new transmission infrastructure expected to be developed during the lifetime of this forum is likely to be located in the east of Lewis, we would particularly welcome applications from individuals who have knowledge of that area.

**The Opportunity**

The forum will help direct significant investment into communities in the Western Isles by assessing and deciding on funding applications.  The Lewis Hub Local Fund will support projects that deliver meaningful impact, build long term legacy and address at least one of the following priorities:

* Health and wellbeing (including tackling social isolation and intergenerational projects)

* Accessible / affordable activities for children and young people (including activities, equipment and travel)

* Community-led facilities and amenities (including community centres and leisure/gym/sports venues)

* Capacity building of community bodies (including funding for skills development and people)

This first local fund is targeted at communities closest to the infrastructure:  North Lochs, Stornoway, Laxdale and Sandwick.

**Who Can Apply**

No previous forum or panel experience is required.  We want to build a diverse forum who can also bring knowledge of the area and fund themes.  We welcome applications from people who:

* Are resident in the Western Isles

* Can support this and future Western Isles’ fund development

* Have experience in, or supporting, the community or voluntary sector

* Have knowledge of at least one of the fund themes

* Support a commitment to social value

* Work collaboratively with others

* Are comfortable giving and receiving challenge

* Can advocate for the fund and its aims

Due to UK Government guidance, Community Councillors, local authority staff member or elected member cannot be members of the forum. If you are currently in one of these categories, you cannot apply even if you plan to stand down upon selection for the forum.

**What You’ll Commit To**

The forum will meet at least once a year, but the role involves more than attending a single meeting.  You will also need time to prepare, read papers, take part in an induction training, engage in discussions, and occasionally support press or community opportunities. Meetings may be in-person in Lewis, online, or hybrid.  Forum members serve a five-year term and receive a fee of £1,000 per year for their contribution.

You will receive a full induction and training from our Community Investment Team who have many years of experience in delivering funds, and they’ll continue to provide support and guidance as needed.

**More About the Lewis Hub Local Fund**

The local fund launches in late 2026. SSEN Transmission has carried out considerable community engagement to inform the focus of the fund.  Community feedback has shaped its design, including a minimum five-year duration and a flexible approach to grant sizes.

**To apply, please provide a cover letter setting out any community / voluntary experience and / or experience with the fund themes.**

We’re Standard Life, a retirement specialist focused entirely on retirement savings and income. We champion the belief that everyone’s journey to and through retirement can be better, and for more than 200 years, we’ve been helping our customers plan and prepare for their financial futures.

Life today is increasingly complicated, uncertain and unpredictable. People move through different careers, face unexpected moments and navigate important choices. Joining our Individual Annuity Pricing team, you’ll gain hands-on exposure across our Lifetime and Fixed-Term Annuity products, combining market insight, customer behaviour and actuarial analysis to help shape how we compete and grow.

It’s a role with plenty of breadth and opportunity to make an impact. You’ll analyse how our products are performing, understand what’s happening across the market and turn complex data into meaningful commercial insight. You’ll also contribute to the development of our pricing approach, assumptions, tools and products, building both your technical expertise and broader commercial understanding as your career develops.

* Produce pricing MI and turn data into clear commercial insight and recommendations
* Implement pricing changes within production environments, ensuring accuracy and appropriate controls
* Support the development and review of pricing bases and assumptions
* Contribute to the ongoing development and enhancement of our Lifetime and Fixed-Term Annuity products
* Undertake pricing calculations and analyse proposition, market and business data to support decision-making
* Make recommendations to senior colleagues based on your analysis and emerging market insight
* Identify and implement opportunities to improve our tools, processes and overall pricing capability
* Collaborate with colleagues across the business, developing your understanding of how pricing decisions support our wider commercial ambitions

* Part-qualified actuarial status, with relevant insurance experience and a commitment to achieving full qualification, which we’ll support you with

Working closely with operational leaders, bid teams, finance, business development and project delivery teams, you could play a key role in analysing bid and commercial data, developing pricing and financial models, and turning complex information into clear, actionable insight.

## Vacancy Information

This role is within a unit where Surrey Police and Sussex Police work in collaboration, whilst remaining two separate legal entities/employers with different terms and conditions.

Both Surrey Police staff and Sussex Police staff are employed in this unit on their own force terms and conditions.

Working Hours - 37.0 Hours per Week   
Shift Allowance - Yes

Location - Haywards Heath

***The starting salary for this role will usually be at the bottom of the salary range and will be pro-rata if the working hours are less than full time.***

## Chief Constables' Message

We really welcome your interest in joining our Police Force. It is a privilege to lead the teams in Surrey Police and Sussex Police who continuously work selflessly and tirelessly in order to keep people in our counties safe.

We are looking for talented and inspirational people who put the needs of the public at the heart of everything that they do and who want to make a difference. If you feel you are that person then we want to hear from you.

We wish you all the very best with your application.

**Chief Constable Tim De Meyer & Chief Constable Jo Shiner**

## The Role & Key Responsibilities

The Serious Collision Investigation Unit (SCIU) is a specialist collaborated unit within Operations Command, responsible for investigating all fatal road traffic collisions, as well as some life-changing injury collisions.

This is a challenging and rewarding role, offering the opportunity to bring offenders to justice while providing support, reassurance and a sense of closure to bereaved families and victims during some of the most difficult periods of their lives.

We are seeking a highly motivated Police Staff Investigator to investigate serious and complex cases from initial handover through to conclusion. Many of the offences investigated by the unit carry sentences of up to life imprisonment.

The role operates a four-week shift pattern (Monday – Sunday), with weekend working on a one-in-four basis.

Week 1: 07x16 / 07x16 / 07x16 / 07x16 / 07x16 / RD / RD

Week 2: 07x16 / 07x16 / 07x16 / RD / RD / 08x16 / 08x16

Week 3: 07x16 / RD / RD / 07x16 / 07x16 / RD / RD

Week 4: 13x22 / 13x22 / 13x22 / 13x22 / 11x20 / RD / RD

We support some agile and flexible working where operational requirements permit. Requests for flexible working arrangements will be considered in accordance with operational need.

**Key Responsibilities**

As a Police Staff Investigator with SCIU, you will:

* Perform the role of Officer in the Case (OIC), managing a caseload of serious and complex investigations.
* Attend collision scenes to provide investigative support when required.
* Progress lines of enquiry under the direction of the lead investigator (DS) or SIO.
* Maintain accurate, comprehensive, and auditable records of actions and inquiries.
* Manage contact with victims and bereaved families where a FLO is not deployed.
* Interview witnesses and obtain detailed evidential statements.
* Interview suspects, manage disclosure, and deal with legal representatives.
* Attend forensic post-mortem examinations, and brief forensic pathologists.
* Liaise effectively with other departments, such as Coroners Officers, Forensic Collision Investigators, Forensic Hub, DFT, Media, Intel, DVLA, HSE, NCA and Expert Witnesses.
* Meet with bereaved families and victims to update them on the progress of investigations.
* Prepare high-quality case files and evidential summaries for submission to the CPS, responding promptly to action plans where required.
* Liaise with CPS Lawyers and counsel to ensure cases are trial ready.
* Submit case material and summaries to HM Coroner and attend Inquests and give evidence if required.
* Attend Crown Court and other court hearings, providing professional evidence throughout criminal proceedings.

## Skills & Experience

This is a demanding but highly rewarding role. Applicants should recognise the post involves regular exposure to traumatic incidents and close engagement with bereaved families and victims during life-changing events.

Successful applicants will demonstrate:

* A high degree of resilience, professionalism, and emotional intelligence. Welfare support is provided through line management and Occupational health screening.
* Proven investigative ability, and a strong investigative mindset, with the potential to develop these skills further within a specialist environment.
* Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to analyse complex evidence.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* The ability to work independently, prioritise competing demands and manage a complex workload with minimal supervision.
* Flexibility to work outside of normal working hours where operational requirements dictate.
* The ability to work collaboratively within a multi-disciplinary team, recognising and valuing the contribution of colleagues and partners.
* Good IT skills, with experience of Police systems including Niche, NICE Investigate, SharePoint, STORM, MS Word and MS Excel.
* A sound working knowledge of the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act (CPIA) and disclosure obligations.
* A full UK driving licence and at least a current Basic Driving Authority (BDA) - or the ability to pass a basic driving assessment.

## Why Work With Us?

Policing is an exciting 24/7 business and we all have commitments outside work. We’re invested in supporting people to balance their life with work and we encourage flexible working. We are open to conversations about job shares and part time working. We encourage agile working, giving you the opportunity to manage your own diary and work wherever you give the best service to the public. This may include flexi-time and home working.

We take pride in looking after our people and offer a variety of benefits;

* career progression
* contributory pension scheme (LGPS)
* generous annual leave allowance
* discounts for everyday spend
* on-site gyms and a range of sports clubs
* generous and supportive parental leave
* financial and mental wellbeing guidance and support

## Vacancy Information

We are opening our recruitment for Police Community Support Officers (PCSOs) and we want you to join us on East Sussex Division.

As the key link with communities across Sussex, our PCSOs play a critical and visible role in helping keep our communities safe, identifying and protecting the most vulnerable and preventing harm. You will require excellent communication skills, a good listener, calm, confident and compassionate. Above all, you’ll simply care about the community and want to do what you can to keep it safe. The role of a PCSO can be challenging, but also incredibly rewarding. If you want to help keep your community safe, then join us now and help make a difference, together.

In return, we offer you a good starting salary, great training experiences, opportunities for progression, and to achieve a professional qualification - Level 4 Diploma in Community Policing Practice – with the pride and personal reward that comes from helping others. We wish you all the very best with your application.

**Chief Constable Tim De Meyer & Chief Constable Jo Shiner**

## The Role & Key Responsibilities

Our PCSOs play a vital part in keeping Sussex safe.

Being a PCSO offers a challenging, yet incredibly rewarding career. Working alongside our policing prevention teams to prevent and tackle local issues; you will be out and about on the streets of Sussex, building relationships within the community and winning the trust of the public.

You will encounter a range of situations from dealing with anti-social behaviour, taking statements from victims of crimes, providing reassurance and helping resolve community challenges. As a PCSO you are the face of local policing for the community, ensuring we meet our policing priorities. There are a range of duties/responsibilities some are listed below:

* Going on highly visible foot patrols.
* Reassuring the public after minor crimes or anti-social behaviour.
* Building relationships with community, religious and business leaders.
* Working with young people and local schools.
* Making house visits to gather intelligence.
* Collecting CCTV evidence.
* Carrying out missing person enquiries.
* Protecting crime scenes until police officers arrive.
* Providing crime prevention and personal safety advice.
* Offering support at large public gatherings, such as sports events and public demonstrations.

While PCSOs do not have powers of arrest and are not involved in interviewing or processing prisoners, they do have the power for a wide range of situations including issuing fixed penalty notices, requiring contact details and seizing drugs. You can find out more about PCSO powers **here**.

By successfully completing the recruitment process, you will join Sussex Police as a PCSO through our new 12-month apprenticeship programme. This will give you the best possible training and, upon successful completion, you will achieve a Level 4 Diploma in Community Policing Practice – equivalent to a Higher National Certificate (HNC), foundation degree or the first year of an undergraduate degree.

## Skills & Experience

To apply you must:

* Be aged 17 at date of application, you must be 18 before you start – no upper age limit.
* Have lived in the UK for three continuous years immediately prior to application.
* Have leave to enter or leave to remain and work in the UK for an indefinite period.
* Meet the apprenticeship English and Maths eligibility requirements - Candidates aged 19 and over are not required to hold GCSE English or Maths (or equivalent) before applying. Candidates aged 16-18 may be required to complete Functional Skills as part of the apprenticeship if they do not already hold the required qualifications.
* Have a full UK manual driving licence (by the time of appointment).
* Not be a current or previous member of a proscribed terrorist organisation or group.
* Not have tattoos which could cause offence.
* Not have six penalty points or more.
* Not have served a prison sentence.

* Fully-funded professional qualification – Level 4 Diploma in Community Policing Practice.

It is anticipated that successful applicants will join us on training intakes in June 2027 or October 2027. **Our Mission**

Swapcard is the leading AI-powered event platform designed to drive revenue growth and foster meaningful connections at in-person and hybrid events. We recognize the importance of teamwork in successful events; that's why Swapcard is fueled by a team of innovators who are passionate about helping organizers build future-proof events.

**Our Vision**

At Swapcard, we believe in the power of meaningful connections. This belief fuels our commitment to pioneering modern solutions that empower organizers to create engaging event experiences.

Guided by our commitment to excellence and collaboration, we aim to redefine the landscape of event technology, setting new standards for engagement, accessibility, and impact.

**Our Beliefs**

At Swapcard, diversity is at the core of our success. With 42 nationalities represented among our 180+ team members, we champion diversity as a catalyst for creativity, collaboration, and unparalleled innovation.

We believe that by embracing a multitude of backgrounds, cultures, and viewpoints, we can truly understand and cater to the needs of our global community of event organizers and participants.

Our full remote opportunities empower our team to thrive, no matter where they are in the world, fostering a culture of flexibility and inclusion.

Swapcard is the platform behind some of the largest trade shows, conferences and association events in the world, and our Customer Account Managers own the relationship with the organisers who run them.

We're investing in the next stage of that relationship: growth. Our clients don't run one event — they run portfolios, sometimes more than a hundred events, each with its own calendar, its own team and its own decision points. Growing alongside them at that scale is a discipline in its own right: a repeatable motion, a shared qualification standard, and a rhythm built around the client's event cycle rather than our fiscal quarters.

The CAM team sits inside our Customer organisation, alongside Solution Design, Implementation and Support. Whoever leads it works shoulder to shoulder with the teams that scope, deliver and support everything the CAMs sell.

Today, two team leads run the CAM function reporting directly into leadership. As we accelerate the growth motion, we want a single senior leader to bring that work together — someone who builds the playbook with the team, coaches them on live calls, and holds a clear analytical view of where the opportunity sits. That's the role.

### Scope

* **Portfolio.** 500+ events across our installed base, run by organisers whose portfolios range from a handful of events to well over a hundred.
* **Team.** 10+ people spread between the US and Europe. Two CAM leads report to you directly who run the rest of the team.
* **Target.** +20% growth on the installed base, delivered through an account-based strategy.
* **Two levers.** Higher penetration of each client's event portfolio, and upsell of digital add-ons and additional modules on the events already running on Swapcard.
* **Mandate.** Renew, expand, and prevent churn and downsell.

### Responsibilities

* **Lead the CAM team.** You'll lead the Customer Account Manager teams across North America and EMEA through your Strategic Account Managers and Team Leads, and set the standard for the wider CAM organisation.
* **Own the number.** Carry the +20% growth target and build the account-based plan behind it: which accounts, which events inside their portfolio, which modules, in which order, and what has to be true for each to land.
* **Protect the base.** Churn and downsell are rarely a surprise to someone who is looking. Build the early-warning discipline, get ahead of the competitive and budget conversations, and treat renewal as a managed motion rather than a date on a calendar.
* **Build the growth motion.** Shape the qualification standard the team works to, the criteria that let an opportunity enter the forecast, and the discipline that keeps the picture current. You'll define what counts as good evidence and help the team hold to it consistently.
* **Coach on live calls.** Join discovery calls alongside the CAMs, debrief together afterwards, and help shape how the next conversation goes. This is where most of the value of the role sits. We expect a lot of hands-on coaching.
* **Own the KPIs and the weekly rhythm.** Activity, contact creation, qualification progress, outreach, forecast. You'll build the pack, read it before anyone else does, and bring attention to where it's needed early rather than explaining it late.

# SaaS Portfolio Sales Advisor (Remote | 100% FTE or Fractional)

**🧬 About us**  
  
With more than 60 SaaS and hosting brands, 4,000+ employees, operations across 23 European countries, and 3.5 million customers, team.blue is one of Europe's leading digital service providers, empowering businesses with the tools they need to succeed online.

We place values such as privacy, transparency, innovation, and local customer support at the heart of everything we do, delivering trusted digital solutions tailored to local market needs.  
  
  
❗**IMPORTANT: on the nature of this role**❗  
  
**This is a hands-on advisory role, not an operating one** (you will not carry a number, own a P&L, or manage the companies’ sales teams. This role does not include commission or variable pay tied to a single company’s performance. If you would miss these responsibilities, this is not the role for you).

**The profile that thrives in this role is a senior operator who has earned their stripes running sales, and who now gets more satisfaction from developing other leaders and businesses across a portfolio than from owning a single company’s quota.**

What this role offers is influence across a portfolio of businesses, freedom from single-company politics, and real flexibility in how and when you work. Your job is to make our companies’ own sales leaders succeed by advising and coaching: success looks like a Head of Sales who runs a better business because you were there.  
  
  
**🎯 Mission & Core Purpose**

As a Portfolio Sales Advisor, you will report to the Director of Growth and work for the SaaS division (a €300m ca revenue group of +15 software businesses, built through acquisition and spanning a wide range of products and markets, from social media management to point of sale) directly inside our companies (one or two at a time) to diagnose and improve their sales go-to-market. We are building a small central capability to support the sales and go-to-market performance of these businesses. This role is the senior advisory part of that: a proven sales leader who helps our companies’ own sales leaders get materially better.

You will embed with a company’s CEO and head of sales for a focused period, understand how they identify their ideal customers, how their funnel works end to end, how their team is structured and how they sell, and then help them fix what is holding them back and build what they are missing.  
  
  
**💼 Key Responsibilities**  
  
**- Diagnose:** focus on one or two companies at a time, embedding for a defined period of several months. Assess a company’s sales go-to-market quickly and honestly: ICP and segmentation, pipeline and conversion, team structure and roles, forecasting, and where revenue is leaking.  
- **Coach and build:** work alongside each company’s CEO and Head of Sales to fix what is broken and build what is missing, staying long enough to make the change stick rather than handing over a slide deck and leaving. Authority comes from the mandate the division gives the role and from your own credibility as someone who has done the job, not from a reporting line. Central performance visibility, dashboards, and sales tooling are handled separately within the team. This role is the subject-matter expert, not the data engineer: you use the numbers; you do not build the pipes.  
- **Develop leaders:** many of our sales leaders have grown into the role from within their company. A large part of this job is developing them: raising their game, not replacing them.  
- **Bring the outside in:** carry modern sales best practices from company to company, so the portfolio compounds what works rather than each business learning it alone.  
- **Flag honestly:** give the division a clear, unemotional read on where each company you work with genuinely stands, and where intervention will and will not pay off.  
  
  
**💡** **Experience & Skills**

- **Sales leadership at scale:** +10 years and a proven track record as a senior sales leader (VP of Sales, Sales Director, CRO, or equivalent) in B2B SaaS leadership roles with a European market focus and across more than one business or sales model, having carried and scaled a sales organisation (you have built pipeline, structured teams, fixed forecasting, and lived the problems you will be helping others solve).  
- **Advisory temperament:** genuine coach and developer of people skills, patient enough to build up a less experienced sales leader rather than talk over them. Credibility and presence to earn the trust of a company’s CEO and Head of Sales quickly, and to be listened to because of what you have done, not the title you hold. You are comfortable being accountable without being responsible, and effective without a reporting line.  
- **Practical fit:** working knowledge of modern sales operations, HubSpot and Salesforce environments, and the metrics that matter, enough to diagnose and advise credibly. You will not be asked to build or administer the tooling.  
- Happy to travel to and spend focused time inside our companies.  
- Full professional proficiency in English.  
  
  
👤 **Added Values**  
  
**- Low ego, high credibility:** you build trust with a wide range of people and let your work show your strengths rather than telling people about them.  
- **Honest and direct:** you speak the truth as you see it, kindly and clearly, and you present it with data rather than opinion.  
- **Comfortable with ambiguity:** you can walk into a business you do not know, orient fast, and be useful quickly.  
- **Motivated by breadth:** you are energised by helping several businesses improve, and you value scope and flexibility over the ownership and comp of a single-company operating seat.  
  
  
⏱️ **Flexible 100% FTE or Fractional**  
  
We are open to this role being full-time or fractional. For the right senior operator who values flexibility, an arrangement of two to three days a week across the portfolio may suit both sides well.  
  
  
**🌐 Location**  
  
This is a remote-friendly function: you can work from wherever you're most productive in the world.  
For those based near one of our offices, if you enjoy a mix of remote and in-person work, you are welcome to take advantage of them.  
Wherever you’re based, this role involves working within a ±2 CET time frame to stay closely aligned with the rest of the team and make collaboration easy.

About Teton
On a night shift, three carers can be responsible for a hundred residents, each behind a closed door. Teton tells them what’s going on in every room, so they know who to check on first.
We put a sensor in the ceiling of each room: an infrared camera wired to a small computer. The computer turns what the camera sees into facts, like who is in bed, how fast someone is breathing, or whether someone has fallen. Then the video is deleted.
We train one model in our office and copy it to every device, so every site improves at once. Staff get the facts through a mobile app on the floor, a desktop app for leaders and planning, and a screen on the wall. Around that sits the service: installation, onboarding, training, and a support chat any member of staff can use.
Around 10,000 care staff use Teton in care homes and hospitals in Denmark, the UK, the US and Switzerland. Many of the falls we help prevent come from staff seeing what’s going on and planning their shift around it, rather than from alarms.
The Role
You’ll design the apps care staff use every day, from the alarm a carer hears in the corridor to the overview a regional nurse uses for every home they cover. You’ll report to Julius, who leads design, work alongside Balazs, our other product designer, and build directly with our engineers.
You’ll work with the AI team that trains our models and the engineers who run them at the edge, on what the models can see and how it reaches staff. Few product design jobs sit this close to the technology.
Most of our users are floor staff, and many are new or temporary. Most never go deeper into the app than reacting when something happens, so it can’t have a learning curve. A smaller group of leaders, nurses and physiotherapists dig into the data, and the same product has to serve both.
What you’ll work on:
Agency with oversight. Staff engage when they can act on what they know and are accountable for it, and that engagement is what makes the product work for residents. Leaders and regulators still need to see who changed what, and why. We haven’t worked out how to give staff that agency without losing the oversight.
The same facts at every level. A night carer can finish a shift thinking it went well, then hear from a manager about a problem that was only visible on an executive’s dashboard. Everyone from floor staff to executives should see the same facts about a home, at the level of detail their job needs.
Health data people can read. We track sleep, breathing, movement and more for every resident, but most staff aren’t used to reading a respiration trend. We haven’t solved how to make a month of data useful at a glance.
What We’re Looking For
4+ years designing software people use daily, ideally a product that had to stay coherent as it grew.
Precision. You structure things well: information architecture, states, edge cases, components. You can say exactly what a design does and why.
You go and see. You’ll fly to customers in Denmark, the UK and the US, sometimes for a night shift. You look forward to it, and what you see changes your designs.
You learn how the technology works. Some things are hard for any camera to tell apart, like a visitor and a member of staff. You find out where those limits are and design with them in mind.
You help define the problem. When a brief is unclear, you work it out with engineers and product instead of waiting, then pick what it needs: a site visit, a prototype, or just building it.
You prototype in code. We expect it, and beyond that you can work however you like. If you can also ship front-end work in React or our component library, even better.

## **Your mission**

As an Operations Specialist, you will own the issues that frontline teams can't resolve on their own: complex merchant problems, internal escalations and formal complaints. You'll investigate them end to end, fix what you can, and route the rest to the right team with a clear, evidence-based case.

You will sit between frontline teams and Product, Engineering and Compliance. Beyond resolving individual cases, you'll spot recurring patterns, turn them into product and process improvements, and help build the systems and automations that stop the same issues coming back.

The role is designed to flex across three areas depending on business need: internal operations escalations, Tier 2 merchant support, and complaints handling.

**Investigate and resolve complex cases**

* Take ownership of escalated merchant issues and complaints, from first contact to final resolution.
* Use product knowledge and technical logs to troubleshoot issues independently, across more than one country.
* Gather evidence from internal teams and contact merchants where needed to reach fair, well-documented outcomes.
* Keep accurate records of every investigation and meet team SLAs and personal KPIs, including quality scores.

**Manage escalations and stakeholders**

* Run the escalation process to Product, Engineering and other teams, making sure issues are handed over clearly and followed up on time.
* Explain what went wrong and how it will be put right, in writing and verbally, to merchants and internal stakeholders.
* Escalate high-risk or complex cases to your manager when appropriate.
* Balance the expectations of internal teams with company policy and regulatory requirements.

* Categorise and analyse tickets, complaints and agent feedback to find recurring pain points and root causes.
* Act as point of contact for one or more products, creating a feedback loop into Product and Engineering.
* Produce analytical reports across countries and translate findings into product opportunities and new controls.
* Test new tools, features and pilots, collect reliable data on how they perform, and turn it into action plans.
* Document, build and improve workflows and automations that reduce manual work.

    **What you’ll be doing as Coordination & Planning Manager:**

    As Coordination & Planning Manager, you’ll lead the planning and coordination of power-related activity across Thames Water. You’ll help ensure critical maintenance, resilience improvements and outage activities are planned effectively, delivered successfully and aligned with customer service levels and regulatory requirements.

    You’ll work closely with operational teams across Thames Water to support effective Power Resilience delivery, identify opportunities to reduce potential conflicts and help minimise disruption to capital delivery programmes wherever possible.

    This is a great opportunity to contribute to a vital area of UK infrastructure and make a meaningful difference to customers and the environment.     * Planning team support and leadership: You’ll support, guide and develop the planning team, bringing together Power Resilience engineering, analytics and operational delivery plans to help deliver the Power Strategy.
    * Coordination and planning: You’ll oversee the coordination and planning of power-related field activities, helping ensure work is aligned with SLAs, regulatory requirements and business priorities.
    * Collaboration and integration: You’ll work closely with Power Resilience colleagues and wider teams to keep plans aligned across engineering, maintenance, operations and delivery, balancing operational needs with resilience investment priorities.
    * Stakeholder coordination: You’ll build positive working relationships with internal and external teams to coordinate planned and reactive works, make the best use of resources and minimise service disruption.
    * Performance and compliance: You’ll develop, monitor and report on planning KPIs, budgets and compliance with internal policies and external standards, supporting high-quality planning performance, continuous improvement and shared success.

    * Experience supporting, guiding or developing a team.
    * Experience working collaboratively with engineering, operations, contractor or delivery teams.
    * Experience using digital tools or data insights to improve planning would be helpful, but is not essential.
    * Planning, coordination, technical or engineering qualifications would be helpful, but we also welcome equivalent experience.

    * A good understanding of planning and coordination principles, tools and systems, such as MS Project, SAP or similar.
    * The ability to analyse information, solve problems and make informed recommendations.
    * Commercial awareness and confidence working with information from different sources and stakeholders.
    * Good IT skills, including the ability to use planning and reporting software.

# Glasshouse and Hydroponics Manager

The Newt in Somerset

Galhampton•£40,000•Full time

**Glasshouse and Hydroponics Manager**

**£40,000 per annum plus bonus and fantastic benefits**

**40 hours per week across 5 out of 7 days, including occasional weekend work. Usually Monday to Friday, 7:30–16:30 in summer and 8:00–16:00 in winter. Based onsite - BA7**

**Due to the location of the Estate a driving license is recommended for this role**

**Advert closes: Monday 12 October 2026 at 5pm**

**🔗****Take a look at our website**

**🔗****Read the full job description here**

*Lead the future of flavour – combining innovative growing techniques with exceptional produce, from glasshouse to plate.*

**Our Glasshouse and Hydroponics Manager**

Our Glasshouse and Hydroponics Manager will lead the growing of exceptional tomatoes at The Newt, taking ownership of the crop from planting through to harvest and clearance while helping drive our exciting move into heirloom growing. You’ll manage climate, irrigation, fertigation, husbandry and pest control to deliver outstanding quality and consistency, working closely with the Market Garden team, Head of Food and our chefs to ensure fruit is picked and delivered to our kitchens the same day. Beyond the day-to-day crop, you’ll select and trial varieties, build relationships with growers and our sister estates, and help develop our own distinctive Newt tomatoes over time. With our tomato-growing facilities entering an exciting new chapter, your knowledge, creativity and experience will also help shape how these spaces evolve – combining productive, innovative growing with compelling member experiences and a story worth sharing. Throughout it all, **flavour is the measure**: what matters most is the quality of what reaches the table.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Take ownership of the health, quality and productivity of our hydroponic tomato crop from planting through to harvest and clearance.
* Manage the glasshouse environment, irrigation, fertigation and nutrient solutions to optimise crop performance, flavour and quality.
* Monitor crop growth, fruit development, yield and quality, using data and practical judgement to continually refine how we grow.
* Lead an effective integrated pest management and biological control programme, maintaining excellent crop hygiene and biosecurity.
* Develop The Newt’s heirloom tomato programme, including selecting, breeding and sourcing exciting varieties and leading variety trials.
* Lead and develop the growing team, planning daily and weekly activity around the needs of the crop and managing the growing operation’s budget.
* Work closely with the Head Gardener, chefs and Head of Food to plan production, forecast supply requirements and ensure produce reaches our restaurants at its best.
* Create engaging member experiences through tours, workshops and opportunities to see and taste the crops while helping shape the future development of our glasshouse and hydroponic operation.

**What we can offer**

* A **positive workplace environment** with opportunities to develop both personally and professionally.
* Peace of mind with **Employee Life Cover**, providing your nominated loved one with 2x your salary.
* Support from our **Employee Assistance Programme**, including unlimited 24/7 remote GP appointments for you and your family.
* Look after your wellbeing with **complimentary access to our Spa and swimming pools** and our exclusive benefit of **50% off Spa Treatments**.
* Stay in shape with **complimentary use of our gym and wellbeing classes**.
* Access to our **Cycle to Work scheme**, supporting wellbeing and sustainable commuting.
* **Complimentary staff meal when onsite** – crafted by our dedicated kitchen team, often featuring fresh produce from our estate.
* Enjoy shopping in both our shops on estate and online with **30% discount** for all our colleagues and **free delivery** for any online purchases.
* **Complimentary garden membership** for The Newt and our partner gardens, including the Eden Project, Kew Gardens and The Lost Gardens of Heligan.
* We value your hard work and recognise your achievements through our **colleague recognition programme – Newt Awards**, with the opportunity to achieve amazing rewards, including a complimentary Hotel Stay.
* Discover exclusive perks with **discounted hotel stays for staff**, accompanied by a **30% discount at our restaurants**.
* A team that knows how to have fun with **regular team engagement activities**, including Fun Squad events.
* **Up to 30 days annual leave each year** for our full-time team.

**What we're looking for**

* Practical experience of hydroponic tomato growing, with strong knowledge of crop husbandry and plant nutrition.
* A strong understanding of hydroponic principles, irrigation and fertigation, with confidence interpreting EC, pH and environmental conditions.
* Knowledge of common tomato pests, diseases and physiological disorders, together with experience of integrated pest management and biological controls.
* The practical ability to maintain and troubleshoot hydroponic glasshouse systems, ideally with experience of CEA monitoring and environmental control systems such as TomTech, Priva or Hoogendoorn.
* Strong leadership skills with the ability to supervise, train and develop a small growing team.
* An accurate and analytical approach to crop, environmental, production and yield data, with the ability to use information to improve quality and efficiency.
* A passionate, resourceful and creative approach to growing exceptional produce, combined with confidence engaging members through tours and workshops.
* A degree or equivalent qualification in horticulture or a related subject, equivalent practical experience, or relevant formal training in controlled environment agriculture or hydroponics.

**Where you'll be working**

The Market Garden grows fruit, vegetables, herbs and protected crops for The Newt's restaurants. It includes glasshouses, polytunnels, soil tunnels and outdoor fields, along with the hydroponic glasshouse, which runs as part of the same unit. The team reports to the Head Gardener and works closely with the wider Market Garden team, the Head of Food, the head chefs and the restaurant teams.

We grow what money cannot buy: varieties chosen for how they taste rather than how far they travel, harvested in the morning and served the same day. The hydroponic glasshouse, of around 300m2, produces tomatoes and peppers for the restaurants throughout the year. It runs nine channels: eight lines in the tomato house, six for tomatoes and two for peppers, with the ninth serving the NFT room. On average, the glasshouse produces 7 to 8 tonnes of tomatoes a year. But flavour is the real measure: taste, quality and the story behind what reaches the table.

This is an exciting time to join the team. The glasshouses are being developed into a space that is both productive and open to our members, growing a wider range of crops, with heirloom tomatoes in soil alongside the hydroponic crop.

**Who are we- The Newt in Somerset**

Nestled within an expanse of rolling fields and steeped in ancient history, our luxury country estate stands as a haven of refined elegance, inviting guests to explore acres of captivating gardens, meandering pathways, and enriching exhibitions - accessible 364 days a year for our members. Our hotel extends a warm welcome, offering a home-away-from-home experience where impeccable service flourishes in an ambiance of unassuming sophistication. Beyond the estate, the Newt's essence remains tangible, with our Ecommerce teams delivering our finest products to homes, while media and membership endeavours keep them informed of our latest developments. Behind the scenes, a tapestry of talented teams - from Housekeeping to HR, Finance to Farming - collaborates harmoniously, crafting an unforgettable journey of growth, development, and innovation, where every contribution creates unparalleled experiences.

**The Role**

The Engagement Manager provides the client-facing wrapper around our delivery. The role runs everything around the work - onboarding, coordination, governance, reporting, scope control and commercial hygiene.

This role is practice-agnostic. Engagement Managers work across the full delivery portfolio and are assigned by engagement size, complexity and client profile rather than by technology.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Client Onboarding & Mobilisation**

* Mobilisation: lead engagement onboarding covering access, security prerequisites, environments, tooling and client-side logistics.
* Stakeholder mapping: build and maintain the client stakeholder map, communications plan and agreed ways of working.
* Readiness: clear the prerequisites identified by the Delivery Manager so the team is productive from day one.
* Kick-off: run kick-off jointly with the Delivery Manager, owning agenda, governance and ways of working while they own approach and technical plan.

**Engagement Governance & Reporting**

* Planning: own the milestone plan, RAID log and dependency management, built on the Delivery Manager's technical view and task-level plan.
* Client cadence: run status reporting, steering meetings and service reviews at the agreed rhythm.
* Single view: maintain an accurate, current view of engagement health in the agreed system of record.
* Pairing rhythm: hold a standing weekly session with the Delivery Manager covering progress, risk, scope signals, resourcing, burn and client temperature; share client reporting with them before it is issued.

**Scope Discipline & Change Control**

* Scope Creep: identify scope creep early and raise change requests before unagreed work is absorbed into delivery.
* Impact: assess the plan and commercial impact of change, using the Delivery Manager's sizing, and hand commercial negotiation to Account Management.
* Traceability: ensure commitments made during pre-sales or in-flight conversations are visible, sized and formally agreed.

**Commercial & Operational Hygiene**

* Burn: track spend against budget and flag variance early enough to act on it.
* Timesheets: drive accuracy and completeness across the engagement team.
* Billing: manage milestones and invoicing triggers and provide inputs to WIP and revenue recognition.
* Resourcing: raise demand to Delivery Operations against the skills and shape specified by the practice, and flag changes to that demand as they emerge.

**Client Relationship & Escalation**

* Day-to-day contact: act as the client's point of contact for status, scope, logistics and escalation.
* Triage: route technical and quality issues to the Delivery Manager and their practice; handle engagement, governance and relationship issues directly.
* Joint position: agree a position with the Delivery Manager before responding to any client escalation.
* Protect the practitioner relationship: ensure the Delivery Manager stays visible to the client and speaks to the technical narrative rather than being screened from it.
* Growth signals: surface organic opportunity to Account Management without taking on the commercial conversation.

**Closure & Continuous Improvement**

* Closure: run handover, lessons learned and transition to next phase or run.
* Evidence: capture references, case study material and delivered outcomes.
* Feedback loop: feed practical improvements back into the delivery standards owned by Delivery Operations.

**Key Skills and Experience**

* PRINCE2, Agile/Scrum or PMP certification.
* Engagement or delivery management experience gained in a consultancy, agency or professional services environment, running multiple concurrent client engagements.
* Client-facing confidence: able to chair a steering meeting, deliver unwelcome news and manage senior stakeholder expectations without escalating every decision.
* Influence without authority: effective working alongside senior practitioners they do not line manage.
* Technical literacy: enough understanding to challenge a plan and hold a credible conversation with engineers. Deep specialism in any one technology is not required.
* Commercial acumen: scope and change control, budget tracking, invoicing, and accurate forecasting inputs.
* Governance discipline: structured reporting, RAID and milestone planning, fluent in both iterative and stage-gated delivery approaches.
* Organisation: able to hold several engagements in view at once and stay ahead of each of them.

**Desirable**

* Exposure to technical delivery across more than one domain, such as cloud, data, quality engineering or automation.
* Experience of both project-based and ongoing managed service engagements.
* Familiarity with resourcing, capacity planning or professional services automation tooling.

**How Success is Measured**

* Practitioner time returned to delivery, and reduction in non-delivery coordination carried by Delivery Managers.
* Time from signature to first productive day.
* Forecast accuracy and margin variance against the sold position at engagement level.
* Client satisfaction with delivery, measured separately from the commercial relationship.
* Escalation volume and time to resolution.

At Scale Factory, we believe in recognising and rewarding great work. Here’s what you can expect:

* 25 Days of Annual Leave: Plus 1 extra day every year for the first three years, and a holiday buying scheme.
* Pension Plan: Employer-matched contributions up to 5%.

* Social Events: From annual kick-offs and Christmas parties to team socials and sporting events, we love celebrating success together.
* Training & Development: Tailored learning opportunities and full support for certifications to keep your skills sharp.

· Identify opportunities to increase the wider value of supplier relationships through marketing, partnership and event activity.

· Prepare weekly trading information, reports, agendas and action summaries for relevant stakeholders.

· Use data and AI tools to support clear commercial recommendations.

#### Product Engagement & Sales Enablement

· Work with Marketing, Sales, Training and supplier partners to support campaigns, communications, training, incentives and product experiences.

· Support Travel Counsellor knowledge and confidence across priority product areas.

· Ensure relevant product information and commercial insight is available to support sales activity.

Commercial awareness and an interest in travel products and supplier partnerships.

Analytical and numerically confident, with the ability to interpret data and identify key messages.

Strong communication, organisation and relationship-management skills.

Comfortable working with multiple priorities and meeting agreed deadlines.

Collaborative and able to work effectively across different teams.

Interested in using data, technology and AI to improve efficiency and insight.

Flexible to travel for supplier meetings, events, conferences and training where required

**Financial Analyst – Originations**

  

**Purpose of the role**

To provide dedicated financial screening, modelling and Investment Committee preparation support for acquisition opportunities across Pallas Software Group.  The role matures the financial insights on targets, so that every Portfolio Manager has early access to rigorous, consistent analysis that can advance the PQs and Modelling before handing across to the M&A Execution team for final checking and approvals.

The role sits within the Finance function already attached to the Pallas Portfolio, working across all Portfolio Managers. The resource is deployed flexibly to whichever Portfolio Manager has a live origination or diligence need at a given time, working under the direction of the Finance Director to prioritise across competing demands.

  

**Scope of Coverage**

* Verticals: all software verticals held across the Pallas Software Group portfolio. The role is not dedicated to any single vertical and takes direction from the Finance Director on where to prioritise effort.

* Geography: United Kingdom and Ireland as the core market, extending to other European geographies as individual Portfolio Managers' mandates require.

* Deal types: platform acquisitions and bolt, on acquisitions into existing business units, as directed by the relevant Portfolio Manager.

* Deal size: predominantly owner, managed and founder, led businesses below the size threshold that attracts a competitive banked process.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

## **Screening and origination support**

* Screen inbound and adviser, introduced opportunities, from any part of the group, against group investment criteria and hurdle rates, recommending pursue, watch, list or pass with a written rationale.

* Maintain and refresh target maps and market intelligence for the verticals each Portfolio Manager is actively assessing, using public, paid and proprietary sources.

* Support Portfolio Managers' adviser and intermediary relationships by logging opportunities promptly and coordinating timely follow, up.

* Monitor market events, funding rounds, leadership changes, competitor acquisitions and distress signals and flag relevant opportunities to the appropriate Portfolio Manager.

## **Modelling, analysis and execution**

* Build acquisition models from source data: revenue quality and recurring revenue analysis, customer cohort and churn analysis, maintenance and net revenue retention trends, normalised EBITDA, working capital, cash conversion, IRR and payback under base, downside and upside cases.

* Prepare Investment Committee papers and offer support material, investment thesis, valuation range and bridge, key risks, integration assumptions and returns scenarios.

* Support the central execution team and Portfolio Managers in coordinating due diligence workstreams across finance, legal, technical and people contributors; maintain the diligence tracker and issues log; translate findings into model and price adjustments.

* Support deal structuring: consideration split, earn, out mechanics and metric definition, deferred consideration, escrow and set, off, and operational ring, fence provisions.

* Track post, completion performance against the acquisition model and feed variances back into future underwriting, across all portfolios the role has supported.

## **Pipeline management and reporting.**

* Own pipeline management jointly with the BD Manager: the BD Manager owns origination and outreach volume, this role owns the financial qualification and status of each target, and the two work from a shared, current view of the pipeline.

* Own the capturing of notes and information recorded in the group CRM, on behalf of whichever Portfolio Manager the work relates to.

* Produce a standing pipeline report for the Portfolio and Finance Director covering coverage by vertical and geography, stage conversion rates, and pipeline ageing across the group.

* Maintain a competitive and valuation reference set spanning the verticals in which the group is active.

* Genuine modelling capability — able to build an acquisition model from messy management accounts and a trial balance without a template, and to defend the assumptions in front of an Investment Committee.

Virta Health is on a mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people. Working cross-functionally across the data science, sales, marketing, and product teams, your work will directly shape how health plans, employers, and policy makers perceive and adopt virtual metabolic care.

* Lead the strategy, development, and execution of real-world evidence (RWE) programs and health economics models to demonstrate Virta's clinical and economic value proposition.

* **First 30 Days:** Onboard with the Clinical Research and Data Science teams, establish an understanding of Virta's data pipeline and existing evidence, and review current research compliance and privacy protocols.

**The Role:**

We are seeking a commercially minded Revenue Operations Manager to own the post-sales side of our revenue engine, based in our London office. Reporting to the VP of Revenue Operations and working closely with the VP of Customer Success, you will bridge Sales Ops and Customer Lifecycle Ops - making sure the customer journey from signature to renewal and expansion runs on clean data, sharp processes and well-timed signals.

You’ll be the operational partner to our Customer Success leadership, Account Managers, CSMs and Finance, turning product usage and contract data into early warnings, expansion opportunities and predictable renewals. This is an individual contributor role for someone who enjoys designing the system and rolling up their sleeves to run it.

* Expansion and renewal signals: design and run the signal framework that surfaces expansion, upsell and renewal risk early - combining product usage, conversation insights, customer health data and Salesforce contract data into clear, actionable views for AMs and CSMs

* Automation and escalation precision engine: build customer intelligence automations that route the right alert to the right owner at the right time, with defined escalation paths when an account shows risk

* Entitlements, onboarding, and offboarding: own entitlement accuracy across Salesforce, CPQ and product access - ensuring customers get exactly what they’ve bought, and that downgrades, churn and offboarding are handled cleanly and on time

* Processes and playbooks: design, document and continuously improve post-sales playbooks across onboarding, adoption, renewals and expansion, so our CS and AM teams run a consistent, measurable motion

* Partner with CS leadership on onboarding, engagement, adoption and retention processes, including time-to-value tracking and health scoring

* Run the renewals operating rhythm with CS and Finance - renewal pipeline visibility, forecast accuracy and on-time renewals

* Administer Salesforce CPQ for post-sales motions (renewals, amendments, upsells) and own compliance and adherence to standard policies, ensuring renewal intent is documented well ahead of term end

* Own post-sales systems architecture and data flows across the tech stack, including but not limited to Salesforce, CPQ, Customer Success Platforms, Product Usage and Engagement tools, keeping data clean, connected and trusted

* Work internally with enablement to deliver content to AMs and CSMs on systems, processes and playbooks, so new ways of working actually stick

* Experience with Customer Success Platforms, and other key CS tech stack tools
